title.zh: 卷四百〇六 列傳第一百六十五 崔與之 洪咨夔 許奕 陳居仁 劉漢弼
title.en: Volume 406 Biographies 165: Cui Yuzhi, Hong Zikui, Xu Yi, Chen Juren, Liu Hanbi
title.raw: 卷四百〇六 列傳第一百六十五 崔與之 洪咨夔 許奕 陳居仁 劉漢弼 Volume 406 Biographies 165: Cui Yuzhi, Hong Zikui, Xu Yi, Chen Juren, Liu Hanbi

sentences.zh: 崔與之 洪咨夔 許奕 陳居仁 劉漢弼

translations.literal: Cui Yuzhi, Hong Zikui, Xu Yi, Chen Juren, Liu Hanbi
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuzhi, Hong Zikui, Xu Yi, Chen Juren, and Liu Hanbi

sentences.zh: 崔與之

translations.literal: Cui Yuzhi
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuzhi

sentences.zh: 崔與之，字正子，廣州人。

translations.literal: Cui Yuzhi, styled Zhengzi, was a native of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuzhi, whose courtesy name was Zhengzi, came from Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父世明，試有司連黜，每曰：「不為宰相，則為良醫」，遂究心岐、黃之書，貧者療之不受直。

translations.literal: His father Shiming repeatedly failed the civil examinations; he often said, 'If I cannot become a chief minister, I shall become a good physician,' and therefore devoted himself to the books of Qi Bo and Huangdi, treating the poor without charge.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cui Shiming failed the provincial examinations again and again and would say, 'If I cannot serve as chief minister, I shall be a good physician.' He then mastered the medical classics of Qi Bo and the Yellow Emperor and treated the poor without accepting payment.

sentences.zh: 與之少卓犖有奇節，不遠數千里遊太學。

translations.literal: When young, Yuzhi was outstanding and possessed unusual integrity; he traveled thousands of li to study at the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was exceptionally able and high-minded, traveling thousands of miles to study at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 紹熙四年舉進士，廣之士繇太學取科第自與之始。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxi he passed the jinshi examination; among Guang scholars, obtaining a degree through the Imperial University began with him.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Shaoxi (1193); he was the first Guang scholar to earn a degree via the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 授潯州司法參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed judicial assistant of Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial assistant at Xun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 常平倉久弗葺，慮雨壞米，撤居廨瓦覆之。

translations.literal: The Ever-Normal Granary had long gone unrepaired; fearing rain would ruin the grain, he removed tiles from the government residence to cover it.
translations.idiomatic: The Ever-Normal Granary had long been left unrepaired. Fearing rain would spoil the grain, he stripped tiles from his official residence to roof it.

sentences.zh: 郡守欲移兌常平之積，堅不可，守敬服，更薦之。

translations.literal: The prefect wished to transfer the Ever-Normal reserves; he firmly refused, and the prefect came to respect him and recommended him further.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefect wanted to divert the Ever-Normal reserves, he firmly refused. The prefect came to respect him and recommended him for promotion.

sentences.zh: 調淮西提刑司檢法官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to investigating judge under the Huai West judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as investigating judge under the Huai West judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 民有窘於豪民逋負，毆死其子誣之者，其長欲流之，與之曰：「小民計出倉猝，忍使一家轉徙乎？

translations.literal: A commoner, hard pressed by debt to a powerful family, had beaten his son to death and falsely accused another; the senior official wished to sentence him to exile. Yuzhi said, 'A petty man acted in sudden desperation—can we bear to make a whole household uprooted?
translations.idiomatic: A commoner, squeezed by debt to a powerful family, had beaten his son to death and framed another. The senior official wanted exile. Yuzhi said, 'A petty man acted in sudden desperation—must we uproot an entire household?

sentences.zh: 況故殺子孫，罪止徒。」

translations.literal: Moreover, killing one's own descendant is punishable only by penal servitude.'
translations.idiomatic: Besides, killing one's own descendant carries only penal servitude.'

sentences.zh: 卒從之。

translations.literal: In the end they followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: They ultimately followed his view.

sentences.zh: 知建昌之新城，歲適大歉，有強發民廩者，執其首，折手足以徇，盜為止，勸分有法，貧富安之。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Xincheng in Jianchang, in a year of great famine, some forcibly opened the public granary; he seized the ringleader, broke his hands and feet as a warning, theft ceased, and through orderly relief the rich and poor were settled.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Xincheng in Jianchang, in a year of severe famine some men forcibly opened the public granary. He seized the ringleader, broke his hands and feet as a warning, theft stopped, and through orderly relief both rich and poor were settled.

sentences.zh: 開禧用兵，軍旅所需，天下騷然，與之獨買以係省錢。

translations.literal: When the Kaixi campaign began, military needs threw the realm into turmoil; Yuzhi alone purchased supplies with provincial reserve funds.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kaixi campaign began and military needs threw the realm into turmoil, Yuzhi alone purchased supplies with provincial reserve funds.

sentences.zh: 吏告月解不登，曰：「寧罷去。」

translations.literal: The clerks reported that monthly remittances fell short; he said, 'I would rather resign.'
translations.idiomatic: When clerks reported monthly remittances fell short, he said, 'I would rather resign.'

sentences.zh: 和糴令下，與之獨以時賈糴，令民自概。

translations.literal: When the harmonized-purchase order came down, Yuzhi alone bought grain at the market price and had the people weigh it themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When the harmonized-purchase order came down, Yuzhi alone bought grain at the market price and had the people weigh it themselves.

sentences.zh: 通判邕州，守武人，苛刻，衣賜不時給，諸卒大哄。

translations.literal: As vice-prefect of Yong Prefecture, the prefect was a military man, harsh; clothing allowances were not paid on time and the troops rioted.
translations.idiomatic: As vice-prefect of Yong Prefecture, the prefect was a military man and harsh. Clothing allowances were not paid on time and the troops rioted.

sentences.zh: 漕司檄與之攝守，叛者貼然，乃密訪其首事一人斬之，闔郡以寧。

translations.literal: The transport commission ordered Yuzhi to act as prefect; the rebels quieted. He secretly found and executed the chief instigator, and the whole commandery was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commission ordered Yuzhi to act as prefect; the rebels quieted. He secretly found and executed the chief instigator, and the whole commandery was pacified.

sentences.zh: 擢發遣賓州軍事，郡政清簡。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military commissioner of dispatch for Bin Prefecture; administration there was clear and simple.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military commissioner of dispatch for Bin Prefecture, where administration was clear and simple.

sentences.zh: 尋特授廣西提點刑獄，遍歷所部，至浮海巡朱崖，秋毫無擾州縣，而停車裁決，獎廉劾貪，風采凜然。

translations.literal: Soon he was specially appointed Guangxi judicial intendant; touring his circuit, he even went by sea patrol to Zhuya, never troubling prefectures and counties, yet wherever he halted he judged cases, rewarded integrity and impeached greed, and his bearing was awe-inspiring.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was specially appointed Guangxi judicial intendant. Touring his circuit, he even reached Zhuya by sea patrol, never troubling prefectures and counties, yet wherever he halted he judged cases, rewarded integrity and impeached greed, and his bearing was awe-inspiring.

sentences.zh: 朱崖地產苦䔲，民或取葉以代茗，州郡征之，歲五百緡。

translations.literal: Zhuya produced bitter tea; some people took the leaves as a substitute for tea, and prefectures levied five hundred strings of cash yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuya produced bitter tea; some people used the leaves as a substitute for tea, and prefectures levied five hundred strings of cash yearly.

sentences.zh: 瓊人以吉貝織為衣衾，工作皆婦人，役之有至期年者，棄稚違老，民尤苦之。

translations.literal: Qiong people wove kapok into clothing and bedding; all the work was done by women, and corvée could last a full year, abandoning infants and neglecting the aged—the people suffered especially.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong people wove kapok into clothing and bedding. All the work was done by women, and corvée could last a full year, abandoning infants and neglecting the aged—the people suffered especially.

sentences.zh: 與之皆為榜免。

translations.literal: Yuzhi posted notices exempting all these.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi posted notices exempting all these.

sentences.zh: 其他利病，罷行甚眾。

translations.literal: Other abuses he abolished were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Other abuses he abolished were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 瓊之人次其事為《海上澄清錄》。

translations.literal: The people of Qiong recorded his deeds in a work called Records of Clarifying the Sea.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qiong recorded his deeds in a work called Records of Clarifying the Sea.

sentences.zh: 嶺海去天萬里，用刑慘酷，貪吏厲民，乃疏為十事，申論而痛懲之。

translations.literal: Lingnan and the sea were ten thousand li from the capital; punishments were cruel and greedy officials oppressed the people—he memorialized ten items, argued them through, and punished severely.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan and the sea were ten thousand li from the capital; punishments were cruel and greedy officials oppressed the people—he memorialized ten items, argued them through, and punished severely.

sentences.zh: 高惟肖嘗刻之，號《嶺海便民榜》。

translations.literal: Gao Weixiao once carved them and called them the Lingnan Convenience Proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Weixiao once carved them and called them the Lingnan Convenience Proclamation.

sentences.zh: 廣右僻縣多右選攝事者，類多貪黷，與之請援廣東循、梅諸邑，減舉員賞格，以勸選人。

translations.literal: Remote counties in Guang Right often had right-selection officials acting in charge, mostly corrupt; Yuzhi requested that Xun and Mei prefectures in Guangdong follow the model of reducing examination quotas and reward standards to encourage appointees.
translations.idiomatic: Remote counties in Guang Right often had right-selection officials acting in charge, mostly corrupt; Yuzhi requested that Xun and Mei prefectures in Guangdong follow the model of reducing examination quotas and reward standards to encourage appointees.

sentences.zh: 熙寧免役之法，獨不及海外四州，民破家相望。

translations.literal: The Xining exemption-from-corvée law did not extend to the four overseas prefectures; families were ruined one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The Xining exemption-from-corvée law did not extend to the four overseas prefectures; families were ruined one after another.

sentences.zh: 與之議舉行未果，以語顏戣，戣守瓊，遂行之。

translations.literal: Yuzhi discussed implementing it but did not succeed; he spoke of it to Yan Kan, and when Kan governed Qiong, it was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi discussed implementing it but did not succeed; he spoke of it to Yan Kan, and when Kan governed Qiong, it was carried out.

sentences.zh: 召為金部員外郎，時郎官多養資望，不省事，與之鉅細必親省決，吏為欺者必杖之，莫不震栗。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue; at the time many ministry officials cultivated seniority and did not attend to business—Yuzhi personally reviewed great and small matters, and any clerk who deceived him was caned; none failed to tremble.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue; at the time many ministry officials cultivated seniority and did not attend to business—Yuzhi personally reviewed great and small matters, and any clerk who deceived him was caned; none failed to tremble.

sentences.zh: 金南遷於汴，朝議疑其進迫，特授直寶謨閣、權發遣揚州事、主管淮東安撫司公事。

translations.literal: When the Jin moved south to Bian, court discussion feared they would press close; he was specially granted Direct Bearer of the Hall of Treasured Plans, provisional commissioner of Yang Prefecture, and director of Huai East pacification affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin moved south to Bian, court discussion feared they would press close; he was specially granted Direct Bearer of the Hall of Treasured Plans, provisional commissioner of Yang Prefecture, and director of Huai East pacification affairs.

sentences.zh: 寧宗宣引入內，親遣之，奏選守將、集民兵為邊防第一事。

translations.literal: Emperor Ningzong summoned him into the palace and personally dispatched him; he memorialized that selecting frontier commanders and gathering militia were the first matters for border defense.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ningzong summoned him into the palace and personally dispatched him; he memorialized that selecting frontier commanders and gathering militia were the first matters for border defense.

sentences.zh: 既至，浚濠廣十有二丈，深二丈。

translations.literal: On arrival he dredged the moat twelve zhang wide and two zhang deep.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he dredged the moat twelve zhang wide and two zhang deep.

sentences.zh: 西城濠勢低，因疏塘水以限戎馬。

translations.literal: The western moat lay low; he diverted pond water to block enemy horses.
translations.idiomatic: The western moat lay low; he diverted pond water to block enemy horses.

sentences.zh: 開月河，置釣橋。

translations.literal: He opened the moon river and set drawbridges.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the moon river and set drawbridges.

sentences.zh: 州城與堡砦城不相屬，舊築夾土城往來，為易以甓。

translations.literal: The prefectural city and the stockade cities were not connected; formerly an earthen wall had been built between them—he replaced it with brick.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural city and the stockade cities were not connected; formerly an earthen wall had been built between them—he replaced it with brick.

sentences.zh: 因滁有山林之阻，創五砦，結忠義民兵，金人犯淮西，沿邊之民得附山自固，金人亦疑設伏，自是不敢深入。

translations.literal: Because Chuzhou had mountain and forest barriers, he created five stockades and organized loyal militia; when the Jin invaded Huai West, border people could shelter in the mountains and the Jin also suspected ambush and dared not penetrate deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chuzhou had mountain and forest barriers, he created five stockades and organized loyal militia; when the Jin invaded Huai West, border people could shelter in the mountains and the Jin also suspected ambush and dared not penetrate deeply.

sentences.zh: 揚州兵久不練，分彊勇、鎮淮兩軍，月以三、八日習馬射，令所部兵皆仿行之。

translations.literal: Yangzhou troops had long gone untrained; he divided the Strong and Pacify-Huai armies and on the third and eighth of each month practiced mounted archery, ordering all subordinate troops to follow suit.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou troops had long gone untrained; he divided the Strong and Pacify-Huai armies and on the third and eighth of each month practiced mounted archery, ordering all subordinate troops to follow suit.

sentences.zh: 淮民多畜馬善射，欲依萬弩手法創萬馬社，募民為之，宰相不果行。

translations.literal: Huai people kept many horses and were skilled archers; he wished to follow the Ten-Thousand Crossbows method to create a Ten-Thousand Horses society and recruit the people—the chief minister did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Huai people kept many horses and were skilled archers; he wished to follow the Ten-Thousand Crossbows method to create a Ten-Thousand Horses society and recruit the people—the chief minister did not approve.

sentences.zh: 浙東饑，流民渡江，與之開門撫納，所活萬餘。

translations.literal: Eastern Zhe suffered famine; refugees crossed the river—Yuzhi opened the gates and received them, saving more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Zhe suffered famine; refugees crossed the river—Yuzhi opened the gates and received them, saving more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 楚州工役繁夥，士卒苦之，叛入射陽湖，亡命多從之者。

translations.literal: Chuzhou had heavy labor levies; soldiers suffered and rebelled into Sheyang Lake, and many fugitives joined them.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou had heavy labor levies; soldiers suffered and rebelled into Sheyang Lake, and many fugitives joined them.

sentences.zh: 與之給旗帖招之，眾聞呼皆至，首謀者獨遲疑不前，禽戮之，分其餘隸諸軍。

translations.literal: Yuzhi issued placards to recruit them; hearing the call, all came except the chief plotter, who hesitated—he was seized and executed, and the rest were assigned to various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi issued placards to recruit them; hearing the call, all came except the chief plotter, who hesitated—he was seized and executed, and the rest were assigned to various armies.

sentences.zh: 山東李全以眾來歸，與之移書宰相，謂：「自昔召外兵以集事者，必有後憂。」

translations.literal: Li Quan of Shandong came with his followers to submit; Yuzhi wrote the chief minister: 'From old, summoning outside troops to gather for a task always brings later trouble.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Quan of Shandong came with his followers to submit; Yuzhi wrote the chief minister: 'From old, summoning outside troops to gather for a task always brings later trouble.'

sentences.zh: 宰相欲圖邊功，諸將皆懷僥倖，都統劉琸承密劄取泗州，兵渡淮而後牒報。

translations.literal: The chief minister wished to win frontier merit; the generals all harbored hope. Regional Commander Liu Wan, on a secret order, took Si Prefecture and crossed the Huai before reporting by dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister wished to win frontier merit; the generals all harbored hope. Regional Commander Liu Wan, on a secret order, took Si Prefecture and crossed the Huai before reporting by dispatch.

sentences.zh: 琸全軍覆沒，與之憂憤，馳書宰相，言：「與之乘鄣五年，子養士卒，今以萬人之命，壞於一夫之手，敵將乘勝襲我。」

translations.literal: Wan's whole army was destroyed; Yuzhi, grieved and indignant, urgently wrote the chief minister: 'Yuzhi has held the frontier for five years, nurturing officers and soldiers—now ten thousand lives are ruined by one man's hand; the enemy will seize victory to strike us.'
translations.idiomatic: Wan's whole army was destroyed; Yuzhi, grieved and indignant, urgently wrote the chief minister: 'Yuzhi has held the frontier for five years, nurturing officers and soldiers—now ten thousand lives are ruined by one man's hand; the enemy will seize victory to strike us.'

sentences.zh: 金人入境，宰相連遺與之三書，俾議和。

translations.literal: When the Jin entered the border, the chief minister sent Yuzhi three letters in succession ordering him to discuss peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin entered the border, the chief minister sent Yuzhi three letters in succession ordering him to discuss peace.

sentences.zh: 與之答曰：「彼方得勢，而我與之和，必遭屈辱。

translations.literal: Yuzhi replied: 'They are now gaining the advantage—if we make peace with them, we will surely suffer humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi replied: 'They are now gaining the advantage—if we make peace with them, we will surely suffer humiliation.

sentences.zh: 今山砦相望，邊民米麥已盡輸藏，野無可掠，諸軍與山砦並力剿逐，勢必不能久駐。

translations.literal: Now mountain stockades stand in sight of one another; border people's grain and wheat have all been stored away, nothing to plunder in the wild; if the armies and stockades join to pursue and drive them out, they surely cannot stay long.
translations.idiomatic: Now mountain stockades stand in sight of one another; border people's grain and wheat have all been stored away, nothing to plunder in the wild; if the armies and stockades join to pursue and drive them out, they surely cannot stay long.

sentences.zh: 況東海、漣水已為我有，山東歸順之徒已為我用，一旦議和，則漣、海二邑若為區處？

translations.literal: Moreover Eastern Sea and Lianshui are already ours; Shandong submitters are already at our service—once we discuss peace, how shall the two districts of Lian and Hai be disposed?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Eastern Sea and Lianshui are already ours; Shandong submitters are already at our service—once we discuss peace, how shall the two districts of Lian and Hai be disposed?

sentences.zh: 山東諸酋若為措置？

translations.literal: How shall the chiefs of Shandong be arranged?
translations.idiomatic: How shall the chiefs of Shandong be arranged?

sentences.zh: 望別選通才，以任和議。」

translations.literal: I hope another man of broad talent may be chosen to bear the peace talks.'
translations.idiomatic: I hope another man of broad talent may be chosen to bear the peace talks.'

sentences.zh: 與之自劉琸敗，亟修守戰備，遣精銳，布要害。

translations.literal: After Liu Wan's defeat, Yuzhi urgently repaired defenses, sent elite troops, and posted them at key points.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Wan's defeat, Yuzhi urgently repaired defenses, sent elite troops, and posted them at key points.

sentences.zh: 金人深入無功，而和議亦寢。

translations.literal: The Jin penetrated deeply without success, and the peace talks also lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin penetrated deeply without success, and the peace talks also lapsed.

sentences.zh: 時議將姑闕兩淮制置，命兩淮帥臣互相為援，與之啟廟堂曰：「兩淮分任其責，而無制閫總其權，則東淮有警，西帥果能疾馳往救乎？

translations.literal: At the time some proposed temporarily abolishing the Two Huai pacification commission and having the Two Huai commanders aid each other; Yuzhi told the court: 'If the Two Huai each bear responsibility but no pacification commissioner holds overall authority, when the Eastern Huai is alarmed, can the Western commander truly rush to save it?
translations.idiomatic: At the time some proposed temporarily abolishing the Two Huai pacification commission and having the Two Huai commanders aid each other; Yuzhi told the court: 'If the Two Huai each bear responsibility but no pacification commissioner holds overall authority, when the Eastern Huai is alarmed, can the Western commander truly rush to save it?

sentences.zh: 東帥亦果能疾馳往救西淮乎？

translations.literal: Can the Eastern commander truly rush to save the Western Huai?
translations.idiomatic: Can the Eastern commander truly rush to save the Western Huai?

sentences.zh: 制閫俯瞰兩淮，特一水之隔，文移往來，朝發夕至，無制閫則事事稟命朝廷，必稽緩誤事矣。」

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner overlooks both Huai with only a strip of water between; documents go back and forth, sent in the morning and received at evening—without a pacification commissioner, every matter must be reported to the court and will surely be delayed and harm affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner overlooks both Huai with only a strip of water between; documents go back and forth, sent in the morning and received at evening—without a pacification commissioner, every matter must be reported to the court and will surely be delayed and harm affairs.'

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal then lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal then lapsed.

sentences.zh: 召為秘書少監，軍民遮道垂涕。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice director of the Secretariat; soldiers and civilians blocked the road, weeping.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice director of the Secretariat; soldiers and civilians blocked the road, weeping.

sentences.zh: 與之力辭召命，竟還。

translations.literal: Yuzhi strongly declined the summons and in the end returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi strongly declined the summons and in the end returned.

sentences.zh: 將度嶺，趣召不已，行次池口，聞金人至邊，乃造朝奏：「今邊聲可慮者非一，惟山東忠義區處要不容緩。」

translations.literal: About to cross the ridge, urgent summons followed without cease; at Chikou on the way he heard the Jin had reached the border and entered court to memorialize: 'Of border alarms now to be feared, none is more urgent than arranging the loyalists of Shandong.'
translations.idiomatic: About to cross the ridge, urgent summons followed without cease; at Chikou on the way he heard the Jin had reached the border and entered court to memorialize: 'Of border alarms now to be feared, none is more urgent than arranging the loyalists of Shandong.'

sentences.zh: 前後累疏數千言，每歎養虎將自遺患。

translations.literal: Before and after he submitted several thousand characters in successive memorials, each time sighing that nurturing a tiger would bring calamity on oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after he submitted several thousand characters in successive memorials, each time sighing that nurturing a tiger would bring calamity on oneself.

sentences.zh: 升秘書監兼太子侍講，權工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the Secretariat and tutor to the crown prince, and acting vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Secretariat and tutor to the crown prince, and acting vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 未幾，成都帥董居誼以黷貨為叛卒所逐，總領楊九鼎遇害，蜀大擾。

translations.literal: Before long, Chengdu commander Dong Juyi was driven out by mutinous troops for corruption; chief commissioner Yang Jiuding was killed and Shu was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Chengdu commander Dong Juyi was driven out by mutinous troops for corruption; chief commissioner Yang Jiuding was killed and Shu was greatly disturbed.

sentences.zh: 與之以選為煥章閣待制、知成都府、本路安撫使，至即帖然。

translations.literal: Yuzhi was by selection made Bearer of the Dazzling Chapter Hall, prefect of Chengdu, and pacification commissioner of the circuit; on arrival all was calm.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi was by selection made Bearer of the Dazzling Chapter Hall, prefect of Chengdu, and pacification commissioner of the circuit; on arrival all was calm.

sentences.zh: 時安丙握蜀重兵久，每忌蜀帥之自東南來者，至是獨推誠相與。

translations.literal: An Bing had long held heavy military power in Shu and always resented commanders coming from the southeast; only now did he extend sincerity to Yuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing had long held heavy military power in Shu and always resented commanders coming from the southeast; only now did he extend sincerity to Yuzhi.

sentences.zh: 丙卒，詔盡護四蜀之師，開誠布公，兼用吳、蜀之士，拊循將士，人心悅服。

translations.literal: When Bing died, the edict put all Four Shu armies under Yuzhi's protection; he was open and fair, employed men of Wu and Shu together, comforted officers and soldiers, and hearts were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Bing died, the edict put all Four Shu armies under Yuzhi's protection; he was open and fair, employed men of Wu and Shu together, comforted officers and soldiers, and hearts were pleased.

sentences.zh: 先是，軍政不立，戎帥多不協和，劉昌祖在西和，王大才在沔州，大才之兵屢衄，昌祖不救，遂棄皂郊。

translations.literal: Previously military administration was not established; frontier commanders often did not cooperate—Liu Changzu was at Xihe, Wang Dacai at Mian Prefecture; Dacai's troops were repeatedly defeated and Changzu did not rescue, so Zaojiao was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Previously military administration was not established; frontier commanders often did not cooperate—Liu Changzu was at Xihe, Wang Dacai at Mian Prefecture; Dacai's troops were repeatedly defeated and Changzu did not rescue, so Zaojiao was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 吳政屯鳳州，張威屯西和，金人自白還堡突入黑谷，威不尾襲，而迂路由七方關上青野原，金人遂得入鳳州。

translations.literal: Wu Zheng was stationed at Feng Prefecture, Zhang Wei at Xihe; the Jin burst in from Baihuan Stockade into Heigu Valley—Wei did not pursue from behind but detoured via Qifang Pass up Qingye Plain, and the Jin thus entered Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zheng was stationed at Feng Prefecture, Zhang Wei at Xihe; the Jin burst in from Baihuan Stockade into Heigu Valley—Wei did not pursue from behind but detoured via Qifang Pass up Qingye Plain, and the Jin thus entered Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 與之戒以同心體國之大義，於是戎帥協和，而軍政始立。

translations.literal: Yuzhi admonished them with the great duty of single-hearted service to the state; then frontier commanders cooperated and military administration was first established.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi admonished them with the great duty of single-hearted service to the state; then frontier commanders cooperated and military administration was first established.

sentences.zh: 先是，丙嘗納夏人合從之請，會師攻秦、鞏，而夏人不至，遂有皂郊之敗。

translations.literal: Previously Bing had accepted the Xia people's request for alliance to attack Qin and Yong together, but the Xia did not come and there was the defeat at Zaojiao.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Bing had accepted the Xia people's request for alliance to attack Qin and Yong together, but the Xia did not come and there was the defeat at Zaojiao.

sentences.zh: 與之至是飭邊將不得輕納。

translations.literal: Yuzhi now strictly ordered frontier generals not to accept lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi now strictly ordered frontier generals not to accept lightly.

sentences.zh: 逾年，夏人復攻金人，遣百騎入鳳州，邀守將求援兵。

translations.literal: A year later the Xia again attacked the Jin and sent a hundred horsemen into Feng Prefecture to invite the defending general to request aid.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the Xia again attacked the Jin and sent a hundred horsemen into Feng Prefecture to invite the defending general to request aid.

sentences.zh: 與之使都統李冲來言曰：「通問當遣介持書，不當遣兵徑入。

translations.literal: Yuzhi had regional commander Li Chonglai say: 'For communication one should send a messenger with a letter, not send troops straight in.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi had regional commander Li Chonglai say: 'For communication one should send a messenger with a letter, not send troops straight in.

sentences.zh: 若邊民不相悉，或有相傷，則失兩國之好，宜斂兵退屯。」

translations.literal: If border people do not know each other and there is mutual harm, the good relations of the two states will be lost—you should gather troops and withdraw.'
translations.idiomatic: If border people do not know each other and there is mutual harm, the good relations of the two states will be lost—you should gather troops and withdraw.'

sentences.zh: 夏人知不可動，不復有言。

translations.literal: The Xia knew they could not move him and said no more.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia knew they could not move him and said no more.

sentences.zh: 初，金人既弊，率眾南歸者所在而有，或疑不敢納。

translations.literal: At first, when the Jin were weakened, groups going south to submit were everywhere; some doubted and dared not receive them.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the Jin were weakened, groups going south to submit were everywhere; some doubted and dared not receive them.

sentences.zh: 與之優加爵賞以來之。

translations.literal: Yuzhi generously granted ranks and rewards to draw them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi generously granted ranks and rewards to draw them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金萬戶呼延棫等扣洋州以歸，與之察其誠，納之，籍其兵千餘人，皆精悍善戰，金人自是不敢窺興元。

translations.literal: Before long Jin commander Hu Yanyu and others knocked at Yang Prefecture to submit; Yuzhi saw their sincerity, received them, and registered more than a thousand troops, all elite and skilled in battle—the Jin then did not dare look toward Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jin commander Hu Yanyu and others knocked at Yang Prefecture to submit; Yuzhi saw their sincerity, received them, and registered more than a thousand troops, all elite and skilled in battle—the Jin then did not dare look toward Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 既復鏤榜邊關，開諭招納，金人諜得之，自是上下相疑，多所屠戮，人無固志，以至於亡。

translations.literal: He again posted proclamations on the border to open persuasion and recruitment; the Jin spies learned of it and from then on superiors and subordinates suspected one another, slaughtering many; men had no fixed will, leading to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He again posted proclamations on the border to open persuasion and recruitment; the Jin spies learned of it and from then on superiors and subordinates suspected one another, slaughtering many; men had no fixed will, leading to ruin.

sentences.zh: 蜀盛時，四戎司馬萬五千有奇，開禧後，安丙裁去三之一，嘉定損耗過半，比與之至，馬僅五千。

translations.literal: When Shu was flourishing, the four frontier commissions had more than fifteen thousand horses; after Kaixi, An Bing cut a third; in Jiading losses exceeded half—when Yuzhi arrived, horses numbered only five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was flourishing, the four frontier commissions had more than fifteen thousand horses; after Kaixi, An Bing cut a third; in Jiading losses exceeded half—when Yuzhi arrived, horses numbered only five thousand.

sentences.zh: 與之移檄茶馬司，許戎司自於關外收市如舊，嚴私商之禁，給細茶，增馬價，使無為金人所邀。

translations.literal: Yuzhi sent a dispatch to the tea-horse office allowing frontier commissions to purchase beyond the pass as before, strictly forbidding private merchants, supplying fine tea and raising horse prices so they would not be intercepted by the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi sent a dispatch to the tea-horse office allowing frontier commissions to purchase beyond the pass as before, strictly forbidding private merchants, supplying fine tea and raising horse prices so they would not be intercepted by the Jin.

sentences.zh: 總司之給料不足者，亦移檄增給之。

translations.literal: Where the chief commissioner's grain allowance was insufficient, he also sent dispatches to increase it.
translations.idiomatic: Where the chief commissioner's grain allowance was insufficient, he also sent dispatches to increase it.

sentences.zh: 乞移大帥於興元，雖不果行，而凡關外林木厚加封殖，以防金人突至。

translations.literal: He requested moving the grand commander to Xingyuan; though this was not carried out, he thickly planted trees beyond the passes everywhere to guard against sudden Jin arrival.
translations.idiomatic: He requested moving the grand commander to Xingyuan; though this was not carried out, he thickly planted trees beyond the passes everywhere to guard against sudden Jin arrival.

sentences.zh: 隔第關、盤車嶺皆極邊，號天險，因厚間探者賞，使覘之，動息悉知，邊防益密。

translations.literal: Gedi Pass and Panche Ridge were extreme frontier, called heaven's barriers; he richly rewarded scouts to watch them and knew all their movements—frontier defense grew tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Gedi Pass and Panche Ridge were extreme frontier, called heaven's barriers; he richly rewarded scouts to watch them and knew all their movements—frontier defense grew tighter.

sentences.zh: 總計告匱，首撥成都府等錢百五十萬緡助糴本。

translations.literal: The chief accountant reported shortage; he first allocated one million five hundred thousand strings from Chengdu and other prefectures to help grain-purchase capital.
translations.idiomatic: The chief accountant reported shortage; he first allocated one million five hundred thousand strings from Chengdu and other prefectures to help grain-purchase capital.

sentences.zh: 又慮關外歲糴不多，運米三十萬石積沔州倉，以備不測。

translations.literal: He also feared yearly purchase beyond the pass was not great and transported three hundred thousand shi of grain to store in the Mian Prefecture granary against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: He also feared yearly purchase beyond the pass was not great and transported three hundred thousand shi of grain to store in the Mian Prefecture granary against the unforeseen.

sentences.zh: 初至，府庫錢僅萬餘，其後至千餘萬，金帛稱是。

translations.literal: On first arrival the treasury held only ten thousand-odd; afterward it reached more than ten million, gold and silk in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: On first arrival the treasury held only ten thousand-odd; afterward it reached more than ten million, gold and silk in proportion.

sentences.zh: 蜀知名士若家大酉、游似、李性傳、李心傳、度正之徒皆薦達之，其有名浮於實，用過其才者，亦歷歷以為言。

translations.literal: Famous Shu scholars such as Jia Dayou, You Si, Li Xingchuan, Li Xinchuan, and Du Zheng he all recommended and advanced; those whose fame exceeded reality or whose use exceeded talent he also spoke of plainly.
translations.idiomatic: Famous Shu scholars such as Jia Dayou, You Si, Li Xingchuan, Li Xinchuan, and Du Zheng he all recommended and advanced; those whose fame exceeded reality or whose use exceeded talent he also spoke of plainly.

sentences.zh: 沔帥趙彥呐方有時名，與之獨察其大言亡實，它日誤事者必此人，移書廟堂，欲因乞祠而從之，不可付以邊藩之寄，後果如其言。

translations.literal: Mian commander Zhao Yan'na then had a reputation; Yuzhi alone saw his big talk lacked substance and that he would one day harm affairs—he wrote the court wishing to grant him a temple post and follow his request, saying he could not be entrusted with a frontier command—later it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Mian commander Zhao Yan'na then had a reputation; Yuzhi alone saw his big talk lacked substance and that he would one day harm affairs—he wrote the court wishing to grant him a temple post and follow his request, saying he could not be entrusted with a frontier command—later it was as he said.

sentences.zh: 與之以疾丐歸，朝廷以鄭損代，既受代，金諜知之，大入，與之再為臨邊，金人乃退。

translations.literal: Yuzhi begged leave on grounds of illness; the court sent Zheng Sun to replace him. After he handed over office, Jin spies learned of it and invaded greatly; Yuzhi again went to the border and the Jin withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi begged leave on grounds of illness; the court sent Zheng Sun to replace him. After he handed over office, Jin spies learned of it and invaded greatly; Yuzhi again went to the border and the Jin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 召為禮部尚書，不拜，便道還廣。

translations.literal: He was summoned as minister of Rites but did not accept and returned to Guang by the direct route.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as minister of Rites but did not accept and returned to Guang by the direct route.

sentences.zh: 蜀人思之，肖其像於成都仙遊閣，以配張詠、趙抃，名「三賢祠」。

translations.literal: The people of Shu missed him and set up his image in the Immortal Roaming Pavilion at Chengdu, pairing him with Zhang Yong and Zhao Bian in the Three Worthies Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu missed him and set up his image in the Immortal Roaming Pavilion at Chengdu, pairing him with Zhang Yong and Zhao Bian in the "Three Worthies Shrine."

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，授充顯謨閣直學士、知潭州、湖南安撫使，辭，提舉西京嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, he was granted Bearer of the Manifest Illustrious Hall, prefect of Tan Prefecture and Hunan pacification commissioner; he declined and was made director of the Western Capital Song Mountain Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, he was granted Bearer of the Manifest Illustrious Hall, prefect of Tan Prefecture and Hunan pacification commissioner; he declined and was made director of the Western Capital Song Mountain Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 遷煥章閣學士、知隆興府、江西安撫使，又辭，授徽猷閣學士、提舉南京鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: He was moved to Bearer of the Dazzling Chapter Hall, prefect of Longxing and Jiangxi pacification commissioner; he declined again and was granted Bearer of the Imperial Insignia Hall, director of the Southern Capital Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Bearer of the Dazzling Chapter Hall, prefect of Longxing and Jiangxi pacification commissioner; he declined again and was granted Bearer of the Imperial Insignia Hall, director of the Southern Capital Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 端平初，帝既親政，召為吏部尚書，數以御筆起之，皆力辭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duanping the emperor personally governed and summoned him as minister of Personnel; several times the emperor wrote in his own hand to raise him—he always firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duanping the emperor personally governed and summoned him as minister of Personnel; several times the emperor wrote in his own hand to raise him—he always firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 金亡，朝廷議取三京，聞之頓足浩歎。

translations.literal: When the Jin perished, the court discussed taking the Three Capitals; hearing this he stamped his foot and sighed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin perished, the court discussed taking the Three Capitals; hearing this he stamped his foot and sighed greatly.

sentences.zh: 繼而授端明殿學士、提舉嵩山崇福宮，亦辭，俄授廣東經略安撫使兼知廣州。

translations.literal: He was then granted Bearer of the Hall of Bright Clarity and director of Song Mountain Chongfu Palace—he also declined; soon he was made Guangdong pacification commissioner and prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then granted Bearer of the Hall of Bright Clarity and director of Song Mountain Chongfu Palace—he also declined; soon he was made Guangdong pacification commissioner and prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，廣州摧鋒軍遠戍建康，留四年，比撤戍歸，未踰嶺，就留戍江西，又四年，轉戰所向皆捷，而上功幕府，不報，求撤戍，又不報，遂相率倡亂，縱火惠陽郡，長驅至廣州城，聲言欲得連帥洎幕屬甘心焉。

translations.literal: Previously Guangzhou's Crushing Vanguard army had been garrisoned far away at Jiankang for four years; when withdrawn and not yet over the ridge they were kept to garrison Jiangxi for another four years. Wherever they fought they won, yet merit reported to the headquarters went unanswered; they asked to be withdrawn and again received no answer—so they mutinied together, set fire to Huiyang commandery, marched straight to Guangzhou city, and declared they wished to have the commander-in-chief and his staff to their satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Guangzhou's Crushing Vanguard army had been garrisoned far away at Jiankang for four years; when withdrawn and not yet over the ridge they were kept to garrison Jiangxi for another four years. Wherever they fought they won, yet merit reported to the headquarters went unanswered; they asked to be withdrawn and again received no answer—so they mutinied together, set fire to Huiyang commandery, marched straight to Guangzhou city, and declared they wished to have the commander-in-chief and his staff to their satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 與之家居，肩輿登城，叛兵望之，俯伏聽命，曉以逆順禍福，其徒皆釋甲，而首謀數人，懼事定獨受禍，遂率之遁去，入古端州以自固。

translations.literal: Though Yuzhi was at home, he took a sedan chair up the city wall; the rebels saw him, prostrated themselves and obeyed; he explained the consequences of rebellion and loyalty, and his followers all laid down arms, but several chief plotters, fearing that when settled they alone would suffer, led their men away and entered Old Duan Prefecture to hold out.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yuzhi was living at home, he rode a sedan chair onto the city wall. The rebels saw him, prostrated themselves, and obeyed. He explained the consequences of rebellion and loyalty, and his followers all laid down their arms. Several chief plotters, fearing that when affairs were settled they alone would be punished, led their men away and entered Old Duan Prefecture to hold out.

sentences.zh: 至是，與之聞命亟拜，即家治事，屬提刑彭鉉討捕，潛移密運，人無知者。

translations.literal: By then, on receiving the appointment Yuzhi hastened to accept and managed affairs from home, entrusting judicial intendant Peng Xuan to pursue and capture them, secretly moving supplies—no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: By then, on receiving the appointment Yuzhi hastened to accept and managed affairs from home. He entrusted judicial intendant Peng Xuan to pursue and capture the rebels, secretly moving supplies so that no one knew.

sentences.zh: 俄而新調諸軍畢集，賊戰敗請降，桀黠不悛者戮之，其餘分隸諸州。

translations.literal: Soon newly transferred troops all assembled; the bandits were defeated and begged to surrender; the stubborn and cunning who would not repent were executed, and the rest were assigned to various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon newly transferred troops all assembled. The bandits were defeated and begged to surrender. The stubborn who would not repent were executed, and the rest were assigned to various prefectures.

sentences.zh: 帝於是注想彌切，拜參知政事，拜右丞相，皆力辭。

translations.literal: The emperor now fixed his hopes on him all the more, appointing him vice grand councilor and then right grand councilor—he firmly declined both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor now fixed his hopes on him all the more and appointed him vice grand councilor and then right grand councilor—he firmly declined both.

sentences.zh: 乃訪以政事之孰當罷行，人才之孰當用舍？

translations.literal: He was then asked which policies should be abolished or carried out, and which men should be employed or dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was then asked which policies should be abolished or carried out, and which men should be employed or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 與之力疾奏：

translations.literal: Yuzhi, though ill, forcefully memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Though ill, Yuzhi forcefully memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「天生人才，自足以供一代之用，惟辨其君子小人而已。

translations.literal: 'Heaven produces talent sufficient to supply one generation's needs—only distinguish the gentleman from the petty man.
translations.idiomatic: 'Heaven produces talent enough to supply one generation's needs—the task is only to distinguish the gentleman from the petty man.

sentences.zh: 忠實而有才者，上也；

translations.literal: The loyal and solid who also have talent are highest;
translations.idiomatic: The loyal and solid who also have talent rank highest;

sentences.zh: 才雖不高，而忠實有守者，次也。

translations.literal: those whose talent is not high but who are loyal, solid, and steadfast are next.
translations.idiomatic: those whose talent is not high but who are loyal, solid, and steadfast come next.

sentences.zh: 用人之道，無越於此。

translations.literal: The way to employ men cannot go beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: The way to employ men cannot go beyond this.

sentences.zh: 蓋忠實之才，謂之有德而有才者也。

translations.literal: Talent that is loyal and solid is what is called having virtue and also having ability.
translations.idiomatic: Talent that is loyal and solid is what we call having both virtue and ability.

sentences.zh: 若以君子為無才，必欲求有才者用之，意向或差，名實無別，君子、小人消長之勢，基於此矣。

translations.literal: If one takes the gentleman to be without talent and must seek men with talent to employ, intent may go astray, name and reality are not distinguished, and the waxing and waning of gentleman and petty man has its foundation here.
translations.idiomatic: If one takes the gentleman to be without talent and must seek men with talent to employ, intent may go astray, name and reality are not distinguished, and the waxing and waning of gentleman and petty man has its foundation here.

sentences.zh: 陛下勵精更始，擢用老成，然以正人為迂闊而疑其難以集事，以忠言為矯激而疑其近於好名，任之不專，信之不篤。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has exerted yourself in renewal and promoted the old and mature, yet you take upright men as pedantic and doubt they can gather affairs, take loyal words as extravagant and doubt they are close to seeking fame, employ them without full charge, trust them without full sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has exerted yourself in renewal and promoted the old and mature, yet you take upright men as pedantic and doubt they can gather affairs, take loyal words as extravagant and doubt they are close to seeking fame, employ them without full charge, and trust them without full sincerity.

sentences.zh: 或謂世數將衰，則人才先已凋謝，如真德秀、洪咨夔、魏了翁，方此柄用，相繼而去，天意固不可曉。

translations.literal: Some say the age's number is declining and talent has already withered—such as Zhen Dexiu, Hong Zikui, and Wei Liaoweng, just as they were wielded in office, they left in succession; heaven's intent truly cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the age's number is declining and talent has already withered—such as Zhen Dexiu, Hong Zikui, and Wei Liaoweng, just as they were wielded in office, they left in succession; heaven's intent truly cannot be fathomed.

sentences.zh: 至於敢諫之臣，忠於為國，言未脫口，斥逐隨之，一去而不可復留，人才豈易得，而輕棄如此。

translations.literal: As for ministers who dare remonstrate, loyal to the state—before the words leave the mouth, dismissal follows; once gone they cannot be kept—talent is not easily obtained, yet it is lightly cast away thus.
translations.idiomatic: As for ministers who dare remonstrate, loyal to the state—before the words leave the mouth, dismissal follows; once gone they cannot be kept—talent is not easily obtained, yet it is lightly cast away thus.

sentences.zh: 陛下悟已往而圖方來，昨以直言去位者亟加峻擢，補外者蚤與召還，使天下明知陛下非疏遠正人，非厭惡忠言，一轉移力耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has understood the past and planned for the future; those who left office for straight speech should quickly be sharply promoted, those sent outside should early be recalled, so that all under heaven clearly know Your Majesty does not keep upright men at a distance, does not detest loyal words—it is only a turn of effort.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has understood the past and planned for the future; those who left office for straight speech should quickly be sharply promoted, those sent outside should early be recalled, so that all under heaven clearly know Your Majesty does not keep upright men at a distance and does not detest loyal words—it is only a turn of effort.

sentences.zh: 陛下收攬大權，悉歸獨斷。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has gathered great power, all returning to sole decision.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has gathered great power, all returning to sole decision.

sentences.zh: 謂之獨斷者，必是非利害，胸中卓然有定見，而後獨斷以行之。

translations.literal: What is called sole decision is that right and wrong, benefit and harm, must be settled with a clear view in the breast, and only then carried out by sole decision.
translations.idiomatic: What is called sole decision is that right and wrong, benefit and harm, must be settled with a clear view in the breast, and only then carried out by sole decision.

sentences.zh: 比聞獨斷以來，朝廷之事體愈輕，宰相進擬多沮格不行，或除命中出，而宰相不與知，立政造命之原，失其要矣。

translations.literal: Since hearing of sole decision, court business has grown lighter; the chief minister's submitted nominations are often blocked and not carried out, or appointments issue from the center while the chief minister does not know—the source of establishing policy and creating mandates has lost its key.
translations.idiomatic: Since hearing of sole decision, court business has grown lighter; the chief minister's submitted nominations are often blocked and not carried out, or appointments issue from the center while the chief minister does not know—the source of establishing policy and creating mandates has lost its key.

sentences.zh: 大抵獨斷當以兼聽為先，倘不兼聽而斷，其勢必至於偏聽，實為亂階，威令雖行於上，而權柄潛移於下矣。」

translations.literal: Generally sole decision should take heeding many views as first; if one decides without heeding many views, the tendency must reach partial hearing—this is truly the ladder to disorder; though authority and orders run above, power secretly shifts below.'
translations.idiomatic: Generally sole decision should take heeding many views as first; if one decides without heeding many views, the tendency must reach partial hearing—this is truly the ladder to disorder; though authority and orders run above, power secretly shifts below.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「邊臣主和，朝廷雖知，而未嘗明有施行。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Frontier ministers advocate peace; though the court knows it, it has never clearly ordered implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'Frontier ministers advocate peace; though the court knows it, it has never clearly ordered implementation.

sentences.zh: 憂邊之士，剴切而言，一鳴輒斥，得非朝廷亦陰主之乎？

translations.literal: Men anxious for the frontier speak earnestly—at one cry they are dismissed—is it not that the court also secretly supports them?
translations.idiomatic: Men anxious for the frontier speak earnestly—at one cry they are dismissed—is it not that the court also secretly supports them?

sentences.zh: 假使和而可保，亦當議而行之可也。」

translations.literal: Even if peace could be preserved, it should still be discussed and then carried out.'
translations.idiomatic: Even if peace could be preserved, it should still be discussed and then carried out.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「比年以變故層出，盜賊跳梁，雷雹震驚，星辰乖異，皆非細故。

translations.literal: He also said: 'In recent years calamities have come layer upon layer—bandits leaping, thunder and hail shocking, stars out of place—all are no small matters.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'In recent years calamities have come layer upon layer—bandits leaping, thunder and hail shocking, stars out of place—all are no small matters.

sentences.zh: 京城之災，七年而兩見，豈數萬戶生靈皆獲罪於天者。

translations.literal: Disasters in the capital have twice appeared in seven years—can it be that the lives of tens of thousands of households all offended heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Disasters in the capital have twice appeared in seven years—can it be that the lives of tens of thousands of households all offended heaven?

sentences.zh: 百姓有過，在予一人，此陛下所當凜凜，惟有求直言可以裨助君德，感格天心。」

translations.literal: If the people have fault, it lies in me alone—this Your Majesty should stand in awe; only seeking straight speech can assist ruler virtue and move heaven's heart.'
translations.idiomatic: If the people have fault, it lies in me alone—this Your Majesty should stand in awe; only seeking straight speech can assist ruler virtue and move heaven's heart.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「戚畹、舊僚，凡有絲髮寅緣者，孰不乘間伺隙以求其所大欲，近習之臣，朝夕在側，易於親昵，而難於防閑。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Imperial affines and old colleagues—whoever has the slightest connection, which does not seize the gap to seek what they greatly desire? Attendants morning and evening at the side are easy to grow close to and hard to guard against.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'Imperial affines and old colleagues—whoever has the slightest connection, which does not seize the gap to seek what they greatly desire? Attendants morning and evening at the side are easy to grow close to and hard to guard against.

sentences.zh: 司馬光謂『內臣不可令其采訪外事，及問以群臣能否』，蓋干預之門自此始也。

translations.literal: Sima Guang said, 'Inner attendants must not be sent to gather outside affairs, nor asked about ministers' ability'—the gate of interference begins here.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang said, 'Inner attendants must not be sent to gather outside affairs, nor asked about ministers' ability'—the gate of interference begins here.

sentences.zh: 若謂其所言出於無心，豈知愛惡之私，因此而入，其於聖德，寧無玷乎？」

translations.literal: If one says their words come from no mind, how does one know that private likes and dislikes enter by this path and that sagely virtue is not stained?'
translations.idiomatic: If one says their words come from no mind, how does one know that private likes and dislikes enter by this path and that sagely virtue is not stained?'

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏嘉歎，趣召愈力，控辭至十有三疏。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and sighed in praise, urging summons all the more strongly; he declined to the thirteenth memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and sighed in praise, urging summons all the more strongly; he declined to the thirteenth memorial.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙三年，乃得致仕，以觀文殿大學士提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaxi he was finally allowed to retire, as Bearer of the Hall for Viewing Literature and director of the Grotto Heaven Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiaxi (1239) he was finally allowed to retire, as Bearer of the Hall for Viewing Literature and director of the Grotto Heaven Palace.

sentences.zh: 自領鄉郡，不受廩祿之入，凡奉餘皆以均親黨。

translations.literal: From heading his home commandery he did not accept salary income; all surplus stipends he distributed equally among kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: From heading his home commandery he did not accept salary income; all surplus stipends he distributed equally among kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 薨時年八十有二，遺戒不得作佛事。

translations.literal: At death he was eighty-two; his testament forbade Buddhist rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-two; his testament forbade Buddhist rites.

sentences.zh: 累封至南海郡公，諡「清獻」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Nanhai Commandery with the posthumous title "Qingxian."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Nanhai Commandery with the posthumous title "Qingxian."

sentences.zh: 洪咨夔

translations.literal: Hong Zikui
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zikui

sentences.zh: 洪咨夔，字舜俞，於潛人。

translations.literal: Hong Zikui, styled Shunyu, was a native of Yuqian.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zikui, whose courtesy name was Shunyu, came from Yuqian.

sentences.zh: 嘉定二年進士，授如皐主簿，尋試為饒州教授。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed registrar of Rugao, and soon tested as professor of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiading (1209) he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed registrar of Rugao, and soon tested as professor of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 作《大治賦》，樓鑰賞識之。

translations.literal: He composed 'The Great Order Rhapsody'; Lou Yue appreciated and recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: He composed The Great Order Rhapsody; Lou Yue appreciated and recognized him.

sentences.zh: 授南外宗學教授，以言去。

translations.literal: He was appointed professor of the Southern Outer Imperial Clan school and left office for his words.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed professor of the Southern Outer Imperial Clan school and left office for his words.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，應博學宏詞科，直院莊夏舉自代。

translations.literal: After mourning his mother, when mourning ended he answered the erudite and comprehensive phrases examination; Academician-in-Waiting Zhuang Xia recommended him to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother, when mourning ended he answered the erudite and comprehensive phrases examination; Academician-in-Waiting Zhuang Xia recommended him to replace himself.

sentences.zh: 崔與之帥淮東，辟置幕府，邊事纖悉為盡力。

translations.literal: When Cui Yuzhi commanded Huai East, he recruited Zikui to his staff; on frontier affairs large and small he exerted himself fully.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Yuzhi commanded Huai East, he recruited Zikui to his staff; on frontier affairs large and small he exerted himself fully.

sentences.zh: 丘壽雋代與之為帥，金人犯六合，揚州閉門設守，咨夔亟詣壽雋言曰：「金人忌楚，必未至揚，乃先自示弱，不特淮左之人心動，而金人且驕必來矣。

translations.literal: Qiu Shoujun replaced Yuzhi as commander; the Jin attacked Liuhe; Yangzhou closed its gates and set defense. Zikui hastened to Shoujun and said: 'The Jin fear Chu and surely have not yet reached Yang—yet you first show weakness yourself; not only will hearts on the left of the Huai be shaken, but the Jin will grow arrogant and surely come.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shoujun replaced Yuzhi as commander; the Jin attacked Liuhe; Yangzhou closed its gates and set defense. Zikui hastened to Shoujun and said: 'The Jin fear Chu and surely have not yet reached Yang—yet you first show weakness yourself; not only will hearts on the left of the Huai be shaken, but the Jin will grow arrogant and surely come.

sentences.zh: 第當遠斥堠、精間探，簡士馬，張外郡聲援而大開城門，晏然如平時。

translations.literal: Only send outposts far, scouts finely, pick officers and horses, sound support from outer prefectures, and open the city gates wide, calm as in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Only send outposts far, scouts finely, pick officers and horses, sound support from outer prefectures, and open the city gates wide, calm as in ordinary times.

sentences.zh: 若金人果來犯，某當身任之。」

translations.literal: If the Jin truly come to attack, I shall bear it in person.'
translations.idiomatic: If the Jin truly come to attack, I shall bear it in person.'

sentences.zh: 壽雋愧謝。

translations.literal: Shoujun apologized in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujun apologized in shame.

sentences.zh: 已而金人果遁。

translations.literal: Before long the Jin indeed withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Jin indeed withdrew.

sentences.zh: 山陽兼帥事青州張林請獻銅錢二十萬緡，咨夔謂宜以所獻就犒其軍，如唐魏博故事，使無輕量中國心。

translations.literal: Shanyang also held command; Qingzhou's Zhang Lin requested to present two hundred thousand strings of copper cash. Zikui said the presentation should be used to reward his army, as in Tang's Weibo precedent, so they would not lightly regard the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang also held command; Qingzhou's Zhang Lin requested to present two hundred thousand strings of copper cash. Zikui said the presentation should be used to reward his army, as in Tang's Weibo precedent, so they would not lightly regard the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 帥乃令輸其半，林亦不復來。

translations.literal: The commander then ordered half delivered; Lin also did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: The commander then ordered half delivered; Lin also did not come again.

sentences.zh: 與之帥成都，請於帝，授咨夔籍田令、通判成都府。

translations.literal: When Yuzhi commanded Chengdu, he requested of the emperor that Zikui be granted director of the Altar Fields and vice prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuzhi commanded Chengdu, he requested of the emperor that Zikui be granted director of the Altar Fields and vice prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 與之為制置使，首檄咨夔自近，辭曰：「今當開誠心、布公道，合西南人物以濟國事，乃一未有聞而先及門生、故吏，是示人私也。」

translations.literal: When Yuzhi became pacification commissioner, his first dispatch summoned Zikui from nearby; Zikui declined: 'Now we should open sincerity and spread fairness, unite southwest men to aid state affairs—yet the first word is of a student and old subordinate; this shows people private intent.'
translations.idiomatic: When Yuzhi became pacification commissioner, his first dispatch summoned Zikui from nearby; Zikui declined: 'Now we should open sincerity and spread fairness, unite southwest men to aid state affairs—yet the first word is of a student and old subordinate; this shows people private intent.'

sentences.zh: 卒不受，惟以通判職事往來效忠，蜀人高之。

translations.literal: In the end he did not accept, but only in the vice prefect's duties came and went in loyalty; Shu people honored him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not accept, but only in the vice prefect's duties came and went in loyalty; Shu people honored him.

sentences.zh: 尋知龍州。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made prefect of Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州歲貢麩金，率科礦戶，咨夔曰：「將奉上乃厲民乎？」

translations.literal: The prefecture yearly presented bran gold, usually levied on mining households. Zikui said: 'To serve the court—is this to oppress the people?'
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture yearly presented bran gold, usually levied on mining households. Zikui said: 'To serve the court—is this to oppress the people?'

sentences.zh: 出官錢市之。

translations.literal: He paid from official funds to buy it.
translations.idiomatic: He paid from official funds to buy it.

sentences.zh: 江油之民歲戍邊，復苦餫饟，為請於制、漕司免之。

translations.literal: The people of Jiangyou yearly garrisoned the frontier and also suffered transport of provisions; he requested exemption from the pacification and transport commissions.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jiangyou yearly garrisoned the frontier and also suffered transport of provisions; he requested exemption from the pacification and transport commissions.

sentences.zh: 毀鄧艾祠，更祠諸葛亮，告其民曰：「毋事仇讎而忘父母。」

translations.literal: He destroyed Deng Ai's shrine and changed it to Zhuge Liang, telling the people: 'Do not serve the enemy and forget your parents.'
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed Deng Ai's shrine and changed it to Zhuge Liang, telling the people: 'Do not serve the enemy and forget your parents.'

sentences.zh: 還朝，為秘書郎，遷金部員外郎。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was secretary; promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court, he was secretary; promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 會詔求直言，慨然曰：「吾可以盡言寤主矣。」

translations.literal: When an edict sought straight speech, he said with emotion: 'I can fully speak to awaken the ruler.'
translations.idiomatic: When an edict sought straight speech, he said with emotion: 'I can fully speak to awaken the ruler.'

sentences.zh: 其父見其疏，曰：「吾能吃茄子飯，汝無憂。」

translations.literal: His father saw his memorial and said: 'I can eat eggplant rice—you need not worry.'
translations.idiomatic: His father saw his memorial and said: 'I can eat eggplant rice—you need not worry.'

sentences.zh: 史彌遠讀至「濟王之死，非陛下本心」，大恚，擲於地。

translations.literal: Shi Miyuan read to 'The death of Prince Ji was not Your Majesty's true heart' and was greatly enraged, throwing it on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan read to 'The death of Prince Ji was not Your Majesty's true heart' and was greatly enraged, throwing it on the ground.

sentences.zh: 轉考功員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 轉對，復言李全必為國患。

translations.literal: At court audience he again said Li Quan would surely be a calamity to the state.
translations.idiomatic: At court audience he again said Li Quan would surely be a calamity to the state.

sentences.zh: 於是臺諫李知孝、梁成大交論，鐫二秩。

translations.literal: Thereupon censors Li Zhixiao and Liang Chengda attacked in turn; he was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon censors Li Zhixiao and Liang Chengda attacked in turn; he was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 讀書故山七年，而彌遠死，帝親政五日，即以禮部員外郎召，入見，乞養英明之氣，及論君子小人之分。

translations.literal: He read books in the old mountain seven years; when Miyuan died and the emperor personally governed, within five days he was summoned as vice minister of Rites; on entering audience he begged to nourish bright sagely qi and discussed the division of gentleman and petty man.
translations.idiomatic: He read books in the old mountain seven years; when Miyuan died and the emperor personally governed, within five days he was summoned as vice minister of Rites; on entering audience he begged to nourish bright sagely qi and discussed the division of gentleman and petty man.

sentences.zh: 帝問今日急務，對以進君子而退小人，開誠心而布公道，且言「在陛下一念堅凝」。

translations.literal: The emperor asked today's urgent affairs; he answered to advance gentlemen and retire petty men, open sincerity and spread fairness, and said 'it lies in Your Majesty's one thought firm and settled.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked today's urgent affairs; he answered to advance gentlemen and retire petty men, open sincerity and spread fairness, and said 'it lies in Your Majesty's one thought firm and settled.'

sentences.zh: 又問在外人物，對以「崔與之護蜀而歸，閑居十年，終始全德之老臣，若趣其來，可為朝廷重。

translations.literal: He also asked men outside; he answered: 'Cui Yuzhi guarded Shu and returned, idle ten years—a old minister of complete virtue from first to last; if hurried to come, he can weight the court.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked men outside; he answered: 'Cui Yuzhi guarded Shu and returned, idle ten years—an old minister of complete virtue from first to last; if hurried to come, he can weight the court.

sentences.zh: 真德秀、魏了翁陛下所簡知，當聚之本朝。」

translations.literal: Zhen Dexiu and Wei Liaoweng are those Your Majesty has selected and known—gather them in this court.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Dexiu and Wei Liaoweng are those Your Majesty has selected and known—gather them in this court.'

sentences.zh: 翼日，與王遂並拜監察御史。

translations.literal: The next day he and Wang Sui were both appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he and Wang Sui were both appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 咨夔感激知遇，謂遂曰：「朝無親擢臺諫久矣，要當極本窮原而先論之。」

translations.literal: Zikui, moved by this favor, said to Sui: 'The court has long had no personally raised censors; we must reach root and source and discuss first.'
translations.idiomatic: Zikui, moved by this favor, said to Sui: 'The court has long had no personally raised censors; we must reach root and source and discuss first.'

sentences.zh: 乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「臣歷考往古治亂之原，權歸人主，政出中書，天下未有不治。

translations.literal: 'Your servant has examined through past ages the sources of order and disorder: when power returns to the ruler and policy issues from the Secretariat, all under heaven has all been set in order.
translations.idiomatic: 'Your servant has examined through past ages the sources of order and disorder: when power returns to the ruler and policy issues from the Secretariat, all under heaven has all been set in order.

sentences.zh: 權不歸人主，則廉級一夷，綱常且不立，奚政之問？

translations.literal: When power does not return to the ruler, then rank and grade are leveled alike, standards and constants are not even established—what policy is there to ask?
translations.idiomatic: When power does not return to the ruler, then rank and grade are leveled alike, standards and constants are not even established—what policy is there to ask?

sentences.zh: 政不出中書，則腹心無寄，必轉而他屬，奚權之攬？

translations.literal: When policy does not issue from the Secretariat, then the heart-and-belly has no resting place and must turn to belong elsewhere—what power is there to gather?
translations.idiomatic: When policy does not issue from the Secretariat, then the heart-and-belly has no resting place and must turn to belong elsewhere—what power is there to gather?

sentences.zh: 此八政馭群臣，所以獨歸之王，而詔之者必天官冢宰也。

translations.literal: This is why the eight policies govern the host of ministers, power alone returns to the king, and he who proclaims must be the heavenly official chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the eight policies govern the host of ministers, power alone returns to the king, and he who proclaims must be the heavenly official chief minister.

sentences.zh: 陛下親政以來，威福操柄，收還掌握，揚廷出令，震撼海宇，天下始知有吾君。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty personally governed, authority and blessing's handle have been gathered back into grasp; orders issue from the court and shake the sea and land—all under heaven first knew there is our ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty personally governed, authority and blessing's handle have been gathered back into grasp; orders issue from the court and shake the sea and land—all under heaven first knew there is our ruler.

sentences.zh: 元首既明，股肱不容於自惰，撤副封，罷先行，坐政事堂以治事，天下始知有朝廷。

translations.literal: Once the head is clear, the arms and legs cannot indulge in sloth; secondary seals were withdrawn, advance reporting abolished, sitting in the Hall of Administration to govern affairs—all under heaven first knew there is a court.
translations.idiomatic: Once the head is clear, the arms and legs cannot indulge in sloth; secondary seals were withdrawn, advance reporting abolished, sitting in the Hall of Administration to govern affairs—all under heaven first knew there is a court.

sentences.zh: 此其大權、大政，亦略舉矣。

translations.literal: These great powers and great policies have also been broadly raised.
translations.idiomatic: These great powers and great policies have also been broadly raised.

sentences.zh: 然中書之弊端，其大者有四：一曰自用，二曰自專，三曰自私，四曰自固。

translations.literal: Yet the Secretariat's abuses, the great ones are four: first self-use, second self-monopoly, third selfishness, fourth self-obstinacy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Secretariat's abuses, the great ones are four: first self-use, second self-monopoly, third selfishness, fourth self-obstinacy.

sentences.zh: 願陛下於從容論道之頃，宣示臣言，俾大臣充初志而加定力，懲往轍而圖方來，以仰稱勵精更始之意。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty at the time of leisurely discussing the Way will proclaim your servant's words, so great ministers may fulfill their first intent and add settled strength, punish past tracks and plan for what comes, to match the meaning of exerting oneself in renewal.'
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty at the time of leisurely discussing the Way will proclaim your servant's words, so great ministers may fulfill their first intent and add settled strength, punish past tracks and plan for what comes, to match the meaning of exerting oneself in renewal.'

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 又首乞罷樞密使薛極以厲大臣之節，章三上，卒出之。

translations.literal: He also first begged to dismiss Military Affairs Commissioner Xue Ji to stiffen great ministers' integrity; three memorials, and Ji was finally removed.
translations.idiomatic: He also first begged to dismiss Military Affairs Commissioner Xue Ji to stiffen great ministers' integrity; after three memorials Ji was finally removed.

sentences.zh: 其他得罪清議者，相繼劾去，朝綱大振。

translations.literal: Others who had offended pure discussion were impeached and removed in succession; court standards were greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: Others who had offended pure discussion were impeached and removed in succession; court standards were greatly revived.

sentences.zh: 明年，改元端平。

translations.literal: The next year the era name was changed to Duanping.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the era name was changed to Duanping.

sentences.zh: 咨夔預乞於正月朔下詔求直言，使人人得盡言無隱，又乞令內職任之穹者各舉所知，皆從之。

translations.literal: Zikui beforehand begged that on the first day of the first month an edict seek straight speech so all might fully speak without concealment; he also begged that inner officials of high rank each recommend those they knew—all were followed.
translations.idiomatic: Zikui beforehand begged that on the first day of the first month an edict seek straight speech so all might fully speak without concealment; he also begged that inner officials of high rank each recommend those they knew—all were followed.

sentences.zh: 時登進諸儒，以廣講讀、說書之選。

translations.literal: At the time Confucian scholars were advanced to broaden the selection for lecturing and explaining the classics.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Confucian scholars were advanced to broaden the selection for lecturing and explaining the classics.

sentences.zh: 咨夔言聖學之實，所當講明而推行者有六：一，親睦本支；

translations.literal: Zikui said the substance of sagely learning that should be explained clearly and carried out has six: first, close kinship among the imperial house;
translations.idiomatic: Zikui said the substance of sagely learning that should be explained clearly and carried out has six: first, close kinship among the imperial house;

sentences.zh: 二，正始閨門；

translations.literal: second, correct beginnings in the inner quarters;
translations.idiomatic: second, correct beginnings in the inner quarters;

sentences.zh: 三，警肅侍御；

translations.literal: third, alert discipline among attendants;
translations.idiomatic: third, alert discipline among attendants;

sentences.zh: 四，審正邪用舍；

translations.literal: fourth, careful judgment in employing the upright and the depraved;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, careful judgment in employing the upright and the depraved;

sentences.zh: 五，儲養文武之才；

translations.literal: fifth, storing and nurturing talent civil and military;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, storing and nurturing talent civil and military;

sentences.zh: 六，憂根本無生事邀功。

translations.literal: sixth, worrying over the root and not inviting merit by creating incidents.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, worrying over the root and not inviting merit by creating incidents.

sentences.zh: 又言常平義倉、鹽課及苗稅多取之弊。

translations.literal: He also spoke of abuses in the Ever-Normal and charity granaries, salt monopoly, and seed tax taking too much.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke of abuses in the Ever-Normal and charity granaries, salt monopoly, and seed tax taking too much.

sentences.zh: 京湖以《八陵圖》來上，咨夔援紹興留司奉表八陵及東晉大都督親謁五陵故事，乞先詔制臣往省，俟還，別議朝祭。

translations.literal: Jing-Hu presented the Eight Tombs Chart; Zikui cited Shaoxing's resident commission presenting the table of the eight tombs and Eastern Jin's grand regional commander personally visiting five tombs, begging first that an edict send ministers to inspect; when returned, then separately discuss court sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Jing-Hu presented the Eight Tombs Chart; Zikui cited Shaoxing's resident commission presenting the table of the eight tombs and Eastern Jin's grand regional commander personally visiting five tombs, begging first that an edict send ministers to inspect; when returned, then separately discuss court sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又復以完顏守緒骨來獻，時相侈大其事，咨夔曰：「此朽骨耳，函之以葬大理寺可也。

translations.literal: Again when Wanyan Shouxu's bones were presented, the chief minister exaggerated the affair; Zikui said: 'These are rotten bones—coffin them and bury in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Again when Wanyan Shouxu's bones were presented, the chief minister exaggerated the affair; Zikui said: 'These are rotten bones—coffin them and bury in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 第當以金亡告九廟，歸諸祖宗德澤，況與大敵為鄰，抱虎枕蛟，事變叵測，顧可侈因人之獲，使邊臣論功，朝臣頌德。

translations.literal: Only report the Jin's fall to the nine temples, return to the ancestors' virtue and grace; moreover we border a great enemy, hugging a tiger and pillowing a flood dragon—changes cannot be measured; how can we extravagantly boast of gain from others, making frontier ministers discuss merit and court ministers praise virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Only report the Jin's fall to the nine temples, return to the ancestors' virtue and grace; moreover we border a great enemy, hugging a tiger and pillowing a flood dragon—changes cannot be measured; how can we extravagantly boast of gain from others, making frontier ministers discuss merit and court ministers praise virtue?

sentences.zh: 且陛下知慕崇政受俘之元祐，獨不鑒端門受降之崇寧乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty knows to admire Chongzheng's capture of the Yuan—you alone do not take warning from Chongning's surrender at the Duan Gate?'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty knows to admire Chongzheng's capture of the Yuan—you alone do not take warning from Chongning's surrender at the Duan Gate?'

sentences.zh: 然不果悉從。

translations.literal: Yet not all was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet not all was followed.

sentences.zh: 擢殿中侍御史，會王定入臺察，力詆蔣重珍，咨夔乃按定疾視善良，乞罷之。

translations.literal: He was promoted to palace attendant censor; when Wang Ding entered the censorate and fiercely attacked Jiang Chongzhen, Zikui then impeached Ding for hating and slighting the good, begging his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant censor; when Wang Ding entered the censorate and fiercely attacked Jiang Chongzhen, Zikui then impeached Ding for hating and slighting the good, begging his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 越三日，左遷定，而擢咨夔中書舍人，尋兼權吏部侍郎，與真德秀同知貢舉，俄兼直學士院。

translations.literal: Three days later Ding was demoted left and Zikui was promoted to drafting secretary; soon also acting vice minister of Personnel, with Zhen Dexiu jointly knowing the examinations; soon also concurrently of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Ding was demoted left and Zikui was promoted to drafting secretary; soon also acting vice minister of Personnel, with Zhen Dexiu jointly knowing the examinations; soon also concurrently of the Academy.

sentences.zh: 時咨夔口瘍已深，復上疏謂當引咎悔過，且乞祠，帝曰：「卿在朝多有裨益，何輕去？」

translations.literal: At the time Zikui's mouth ulcer was already deep; he again memorialized that one should accept blame and repent, and also begged a temple post. The emperor said: 'You in court have greatly helped—why lightly leave?'
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zikui's mouth ulcer was already deep; he again memorialized that one should accept blame and repent, and also begged a temple post. The emperor said: 'You in court have greatly helped—why lightly leave?'

sentences.zh: 咨夔奏：「臣數備臺諫、給舍，皆不能遏六月之師，何補於朝？

translations.literal: Zikui memorialized: 'Your servant has several times served as censor and drafting reviewer, yet could not restrain the army of the sixth month—what help to the court?
translations.idiomatic: Zikui memorialized: 'Your servant has several times served as censor and drafting reviewer, yet could not restrain the army of the sixth month—what help to the court?

sentences.zh: 臣病久當去，去猶足裨風俗。」

translations.literal: Your servant has been ill long and should leave; even in leaving he can still benefit customs.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has been ill long and should leave; even in leaving he can still benefit customs.'

sentences.zh: 帝勉留之，遷吏部侍郎兼給事中。

translations.literal: The emperor urged him to stay and promoted him to vice minister of Personnel concurrently reviewing secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor urged him to stay and promoted him to vice minister of Personnel concurrently reviewing secretary.

sentences.zh: 奏：「比徇私成俗，化實未更，所恃以一公鑠萬私者，獨陛下耳，而好樂營繕，親厚近屬，保護舊臣，若未能無所繫累。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'Recently favoritism has become custom and transformation has truly not changed; what alone can melt ten thousand privates with one fairness is Your Majesty—yet love of music, construction, closeness to near kin, and protecting old ministers seem not yet free of entanglement.'
