translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: 'Recently favoritism has become custom and transformation has truly not changed; what alone can melt ten thousand privates with one fairness is Your Majesty—yet love of music, construction, closeness to near kin, and protecting old ministers seem not yet free of entanglement.'

sentences.zh: 上在位逾一紀，國本未立，未有敢深言之者，咨夔乞擇宗室子養之，並為濟王立後。

translations.literal: The emperor had been on the throne more than a decade and the foundation of the state was not established; none dared speak deeply—Zikui begged to choose an imperial clansman to rear and also to establish an heir for Prince Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had been on the throne more than a decade and the foundation of the state was not established; none dared speak deeply—Zikui begged to choose an imperial clansman to rear and also to establish an heir for Prince Ji.

sentences.zh: 擢給事中，史嵩之入相，召赴闕下，進刑部尚書，拜翰林學士、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was promoted to reviewing secretary; Shi Songzhi entered the phase and was summoned to court, advanced to minister of Punishments, and appointed Hanlin academician and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to reviewing secretary; Shi Songzhi entered the phase and was summoned to court, advanced to minister of Punishments, and appointed Hanlin academician and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 求去愈力，加端明殿學士，卒。

translations.literal: He sought leave all the more forcefully, was given Bearer of the Hall of Bright Clarity, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He sought leave all the more forcefully, was given Bearer of the Hall of Bright Clarity, and died.

sentences.zh: 御筆：「洪咨夔鯁亮忠愨，有助親政，與執政恩例，特贈兩官。」

translations.literal: Imperial brush: 'Hong Zikui was upright, bright, loyal, and sincere, aiding personal rule; grant two ranks beyond the precedent for chief ministers.'
translations.idiomatic: Imperial brush: 'Hong Zikui was upright, bright, loyal, and sincere, aiding personal rule; grant two ranks beyond the precedent for chief ministers.'

sentences.zh: 其遺文有《兩漢詔令𢱯抄》、《春秋說》、外內制、奏議、詩文行於世。

translations.literal: His surviving writings include Collected Copies of Han Edicts, Explanations of the Spring and Autumn, outer and inner drafts, memorials, and poetry and prose current in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His surviving writings include Collected Copies of Han Edicts, Explanations of the Spring and Autumn, outer and inner drafts, memorials, and poetry and prose current in the world.

sentences.zh: 許奕，字成子，簡州人。

translations.literal: Xu Yi, courtesy name Chengzi, was a man of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi, whose courtesy name was Chengzi, came from Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 以父任主長江簿。

translations.literal: By his father's official privilege, he served as registrar of Changjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's office, he was appointed registrar of Changjiang.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，免喪調涪城尉。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; when the mourning period ended, he was appointed commandant of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his mother, he was appointed commandant of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 慶元五年，寧宗親擢進士第一，授簽書劍南東川節度判官。

translations.literal: In Qingyuan 5, Emperor Ningzong personally selected him as first among the jinshi and appointed him signing secretary of the Jiannan East Circuit military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingyuan 5 (1199), Emperor Ningzong personally selected him as first among the jinshi and appointed him signing secretary of the Jiannan East Circuit military commission.

sentences.zh: 未期年，持所生父心喪，召為秘書省正字，遷校書郎兼吳興郡王府教授。

translations.literal: Before a full year had passed, he observed heart-mourning for his birth father; he was summoned to be corrector in the Palace Library, then promoted to proofreader and concurrently professor in the household of the Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year had passed, he went into private mourning for his birth father. He was then summoned as corrector in the Palace Library and promoted to proofreader, concurrently serving as professor in the household of the Prince of Wuxing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋遷秘書郎、著作佐郎、著作郎，權考功郎官，非報謁問疾不出。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted secretary, assistant compiler, and compiler; acting director of the Ministry of Personnel—he did not go out except for required visits and inquiries about illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted secretary, assistant compiler, and compiler; acting director of the Ministry of Personnel—he did not go out except for required visits and inquiries about illness.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人，韓侂胄議開邊，奕貽書曰：「今日之勢，如元氣僅屬，不足以當寒暑之寇。」

translations.literal: He was promoted recorder of the emperor's actions; when Han Tuozhou discussed opening the frontier, Yi sent a letter: 'Today's situation is like vital qi barely remaining, insufficient to withstand the raid of cold and heat.'
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted recorder of the emperor's actions; when Han Tuozhou discussed opening the frontier, Yi sent a letter: 'Today's situation is like vital qi barely remaining, insufficient to withstand the raid of cold and heat.'

sentences.zh: 又因轉對，論：「今日之急惟備邊，而朝廷晏然，百官充位如平時。

translations.literal: He also at court audience discussed: 'Today's urgency is only preparing the frontier, yet the court is at ease and the hundred officials fill posts as in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: He also at court audience discussed: 'Today's urgency is only preparing the frontier, yet the court is at ease and the hundred officials fill posts as in ordinary times.

sentences.zh: 京西、淮上之師敗同罰異。

translations.literal: Jing West and Huai Shang armies were defeated with the same punishment differing.
translations.idiomatic: Jing West and Huai Shang armies were defeated with the same punishment differing.

sentences.zh: 總領，王人也，而聽宣撫司節制，或為參謀。

translations.literal: The chief commissioner is the king's man, yet he listens to the pacification commissioner's control, or serves as staff planner.
translations.idiomatic: The chief commissioner is the king's man, yet he listens to the pacification commissioner's control, or serves as staff planner.

sentences.zh: 廟堂之議，外廷莫得聞，護聖之軍，半發於外，而禁衛單薄。」

translations.literal: Court discussion—outer court may not hear; Protecting Sagely troops half sent outside while metropolitan guards are thin.'
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberations could not be heard outside; half the Protecting Sagely troops were deployed abroad while the metropolitan guard was thin.'

sentences.zh: 乞鞫勘贓吏，永廢勿用。

translations.literal: He begged to investigate and try corrupt officials and forever dismiss them without employment.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to investigate and try corrupt officials and dismiss them forever without employment.

sentences.zh: 特與放行以啟僥幸者，宜加遏絕。

translations.literal: Those specially released to open the way for lucky advancement should be further blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Those specially released to open the way for lucky advancement should be further blocked.

sentences.zh: 所言皆侂胄所不樂也。

translations.literal: What he spoke was all what Tuozhou did not like.
translations.idiomatic: What he spoke was all what Tuozhou did not like.

sentences.zh: 蜀盜既平，以起居舍人宣撫四川。

translations.literal: When Shu bandits were pacified, he was made recorder of the emperor's actions to pacify Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu bandits were pacified, he was made recorder of the emperor's actions to pacify Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 奕謂：「使從中遣，必淹時乃至，既又徒云犒師，而不以旌別淑慝為指，無以尉蜀父老之望。」

translations.literal: Yi said: 'If sent from the center, it will surely be delayed before arrival; moreover only saying reward the army without distinguishing good and evil as the aim cannot comfort Shu elders' hopes.'
translations.idiomatic: Yi said: 'If sent from the center, it will surely be delayed before arrival; moreover only saying reward the army without distinguishing good and evil as the aim cannot comfort Shu elders' hopes.'

sentences.zh: 執政是其言。

translations.literal: The chief ministers agreed with his words.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers agreed with his words.

sentences.zh: 又請：「遇朝會，起居郎、舍人分左右立如常儀。

translations.literal: He also requested: 'At court assemblies, recorders of the emperor's actions left and right should stand as in ordinary ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested: 'At court assemblies, recorders of the emperor's actions left and right should stand as in ordinary ritual.

sentences.zh: 前後殿坐，侍立官御坐東南面西立，可以獲聞聖訓，傳示無極。

translations.literal: Before and after the hall sessions, attendant officials standing southeast of the imperial seat facing west can hear sagely instruction and transmit it without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after the hall sessions, attendant officials standing southeast of the imperial seat facing west can hear sagely instruction and transmit it without limit.

sentences.zh: 臣僚奏事，亦不敢易。」

translations.literal: When ministers memorialize, they also dare not change this.'
translations.idiomatic: When ministers memorialize, they also dare not change this.'

sentences.zh: 詔下其疏討論之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his memorial discussed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his memorial discussed.

sentences.zh: 遣奕使金，奕與骨肉死訣，詣執政趣受指請行，執政曰：「金人要索，議未決者尚多，今將奈何？」

translations.literal: Yi was sent as envoy to the Jin; he took leave of kin as if for death and went to the chief ministers urging acceptance of instructions to go; the chief minister said: 'The Jin people's demands—matters not yet decided are still many; what now?'
translations.idiomatic: Yi was sent as envoy to the Jin; he took leave of kin as if for death and went to the chief ministers urging acceptance of instructions to go; the chief minister said: 'The Jin people's demands—matters not yet decided are still many; what now?'

sentences.zh: 奕曰：「往集議時，奕嘗謂增歲幣、歸俘虜或可耳，外此其可從乎？

translations.literal: Yi said: 'At the gathering for discussion I once said increasing yearly tribute and returning captives might be acceptable—beyond that can one follow?
translations.idiomatic: Yi said: 'At the gathering for discussion I once said increasing yearly tribute and returning captives might be acceptable—beyond that can one follow?

sentences.zh: 不可行者，當死守之。」

translations.literal: What cannot be done one should die guarding.'
translations.idiomatic: What cannot be done one should die guarding.'

sentences.zh: 尋遷起居郎兼權給事中，以國事未濟力辭，不許。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted recorder of the emperor's actions concurrently acting reviewing secretary; because state affairs were not settled he forcefully declined—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted recorder of the emperor's actions concurrently acting reviewing secretary; because state affairs were not settled he forcefully declined—not permitted.

sentences.zh: 金人聞奕名久，禮迓甚恭，方清暑，離宮相距二十里，至是特為奕還內。

translations.literal: The Jin had long heard Yi's name and received him with great courtesy; it was midsummer and the detached palace was twenty li apart—now they especially returned Yi inside.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin had long heard Yi's name and received him with great courtesy; it was midsummer and the detached palace was twenty li apart—now they especially returned Yi inside.

sentences.zh: 方射，奕破的十有一，乃卒行成。

translations.literal: During archery, Yi hit the target eleven times out of ten, and only then was the agreement finally concluded.
translations.idiomatic: During archery, Yi hit the target eleven times out of ten, and only then was the agreement finally concluded.

sentences.zh: 還奏，帝優勞久之，奕復奏：「和不可恃，宜葺紀綱，練將卒，使屈信進退之權，復歸於我。」

translations.literal: After returning and reporting, the emperor comforted and rewarded him for a long time; Yi again memorialized: "Peace cannot be relied on. We should repair discipline, train generals and soldiers, and make the power to bend and extend, advance and withdraw, return to us."
translations.idiomatic: After returning and reporting, the emperor comforted and rewarded him for a long time; Yi again memorialized: "Peace cannot be relied on. We should repair discipline, train generals and soldiers, and make the power to bend and extend, advance and withdraw, return to us."

sentences.zh: 客有以使事賀者，奕憮然曰：「是豈得已者，吾深為天下愧之。」

translations.literal: When a guest congratulated him on the mission, Yi said in distress, "How could this have been helped? I am deeply ashamed of it for all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: When a guest congratulated him on the mission, Yi said in distress, "How could this have been helped? I am deeply ashamed of it for all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 權禮部侍郎，條六事以獻。

translations.literal: Acting as vice minister of rites, he submitted six articles.
translations.idiomatic: Acting as vice minister of rites, he submitted six articles.

sentences.zh: 俄兼侍講。

translations.literal: Soon he also served concurrently as lecturer-in-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served concurrently as lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 會諫官王居安、傅伯成以言事去職，奕上疏力爭之。

translations.literal: When remonstrating officials Wang Ju'an and Fu Bocheng left office for speaking on affairs, Yi submitted a memorial forcefully disputing it.
translations.idiomatic: When remonstrating officials Wang Ju'an and Fu Bocheng left office for speaking on affairs, Yi submitted a memorial forcefully disputing it.

sentences.zh: 其後又因災異申言曰：「比年上下以言為諱，諫官無故而去者再矣。

translations.literal: Afterward, again because of calamities and anomalies, he said: "In recent years, high and low have treated speech as taboo, and remonstrating officials have twice been removed without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, again because of calamities and anomalies, he said: "In recent years, high and low have treated speech as taboo, and remonstrating officials have twice been removed without cause.

sentences.zh: 以言名官，且不得盡，況疏遠乎。」

translations.literal: Officials whose posts are named for speech cannot even be fully used; how much less can distant outsiders speak?"
translations.idiomatic: Officials whose posts are named for speech cannot even be fully used; how much less can distant outsiders speak?"

sentences.zh: 又論：「用兵以來，資賞泛濫，僥倖捷出，宜加裁制。」

translations.literal: He also argued: "Since the use of troops began, rewards and bestowals have become excessive, and undeserved advancement has appeared everywhere; restraint should be imposed."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "Since the use of troops began, rewards and bestowals have become excessive, and undeserved advancement has appeared everywhere; restraint should be imposed."

sentences.zh: 夏旱，詔求言，奕言：「當以實意行實政，活民於死，不可責償於禱祠之間而已也。

translations.literal: During a summer drought, an edict sought comments, and Yi said: "One should carry out real government with real intent and save the people from death; it is not enough merely to seek repayment through prayers and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: During a summer drought, an edict sought comments, and Yi said: "One should carry out real government with real intent and save the people from death; it is not enough merely to seek repayment through prayers and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 蝗至都城，然後下禮寺講酺祭，孰非王土，顧及境而懼，偶不至輦下，則終不以為災乎。」

translations.literal: Only after locusts reached the capital did the Court of Rites discuss the exorcism sacrifice. What land is not the king's soil? Should the court fear only when calamity reaches the border, and if by chance it does not reach beneath the imperial carriage, never treat it as a disaster?"
translations.idiomatic: Only after locusts reached the capital did the Court of Rites discuss the exorcism sacrifice. What land is not the king's soil? Should the court fear only when calamity reaches the border, and if by chance it does not reach beneath the imperial carriage, never treat it as a disaster?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「權臣之誅也，下至閭巷，讙聲如雷。

translations.literal: He also said: "When the powerful minister was executed, shouts of joy were like thunder down to the lanes and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When the powerful minister was executed, shouts of joy were like thunder down to the lanes and alleys.

sentences.zh: 蓋更化之初，人有厚望，久而無以相遠也，此謗讟之所從生。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of reform, people had great hopes; after a long time, nothing set the court apart from the past. This is where slander and resentment arise."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of reform, people had great hopes; after a long time, nothing set the court apart from the past. This is where slander and resentment arise."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「內降非盛世事也，王璿進狀不實而經營以求倖免，裴伸何人，驟為帶御器械。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Inner palace appointments are not the business of a flourishing age. Wang Xuan submitted a false report and schemed to escape punishment; who is Pei Shen, that he was suddenly made Bearer of Imperial Arms?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Inner palace appointments are not the business of a flourishing age. Wang Xuan submitted a false report and schemed to escape punishment; who is Pei Shen, that he was suddenly made Bearer of Imperial Arms?"

sentences.zh: 時應詔者甚眾，奕言最為剴切。

translations.literal: At the time many answered the edict; Yi's words were the most earnest and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many answered the edict; Yi's words were the most earnest and cutting.

sentences.zh: 攝兼侍讀，每進讀至古今治亂，必參言時事：「願陛下試思，設遇事若此，當何以處之。」

translations.literal: Acting concurrently as reader-in-attendance, whenever his readings reached ancient and modern order and disorder, he always joined them to current affairs: "May Your Majesty try to think: if you encountered a matter like this, how would you handle it?"
translations.idiomatic: Acting concurrently as reader-in-attendance, whenever his readings reached ancient and modern order and disorder, he always joined them to current affairs: "May Your Majesty try to think: if you encountered a matter like this, how would you handle it?"

sentences.zh: 必拱默移時，俟帝凝思，乃徐竟其說。

translations.literal: He would bow silently for some time, wait for the emperor to concentrate his thought, and only then slowly finish his explanation.
translations.idiomatic: He would bow silently for some time, wait for the emperor to concentrate his thought, and only then slowly finish his explanation.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「如此則經筵不徒設矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "If so, then the Classics Mat is not set up in vain."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If so, then the Classics Mat is not set up in vain."

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎兼修玉牒官，兼權給事中，論駁十有六事，皆貴族近習之撓政體者。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of personnel, concurrently official for revising the imperial genealogy and acting reviewing secretary; he disputed and returned sixteen matters, all involving nobles and intimates who disrupted the form of government.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of personnel, concurrently official for revising the imperial genealogy and acting reviewing secretary; he disputed and returned sixteen matters, all involving nobles and intimates who disrupted the form of government.

sentences.zh: 而封還劉德秀贈典、高文虎之奉祠，士論尤韙之。

translations.literal: He also returned Liu Dexiu's posthumous honors and Gao Wenhu's temple appointment; public opinion especially approved this.
translations.idiomatic: He also returned Liu Dexiu's posthumous honors and Gao Wenhu's temple appointment; public opinion especially approved this.

sentences.zh: 加楊次山少保、永陽郡王，奕上疏曰：「自古外戚恩寵太甚，鮮不禍咎，天道惡盈，理所必至。

translations.literal: When Yang Cishan was made junior guardian and Prince of Yongyang, Yi submitted a memorial: "From antiquity, when imperial relatives by marriage received excessive favor, few failed to bring calamity and blame; Heaven's way hates fullness, and this is what principle necessarily brings.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Cishan was made junior guardian and Prince of Yongyang, Yi submitted a memorial: "From antiquity, when imperial relatives by marriage received excessive favor, few failed to bring calamity and blame; Heaven's way hates fullness, and this is what principle necessarily brings.

sentences.zh: 次山果辭，則宜從之，如欲更示優恩，則超轉少傅，在陛下既隆於恩，在次山知止於義，顧不休哉！」

translations.literal: If Cishan indeed declines, it is fitting to follow him. If Your Majesty wishes further to show generous grace, then promote him to junior mentor; Your Majesty will have shown great favor, and Cishan will know to stop at righteousness. Would this not be excellent?"
translations.idiomatic: If Cishan indeed declines, it is fitting to follow him. If Your Majesty wishes further to show generous grace, then promote him to junior mentor; Your Majesty will have shown great favor, and Cishan will know to stop at righteousness. Would this not be excellent?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「史彌遠力辭恩命，宜從之以成其美。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Shi Miyuan has vigorously declined the gracious appointment; the court should follow him and complete his virtue."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Shi Miyuan has vigorously declined the gracious appointment; the court should follow him and complete his virtue."

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, but there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 奕遂臥家求補外，以顯謨閣待制知瀘州。

translations.literal: Yi then stayed home and requested an outside posting; as waiting appointee of the Manifest Illustrious Hall, he was made prefect of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yi then stayed home and requested an outside posting; as waiting appointee of the Manifest Illustrious Hall, he was made prefect of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 彌遠問所欲言，奕曰：「比觀時事，調護之功深，扶持之意少，非朝廷之利也。」

translations.literal: Miyuan asked what he wished to say, and Yi said, "Looking at current affairs recently, there is much effort at adjustment and protection, but little intent to support and uphold; this is not to the court's advantage."
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan asked what he wished to say, and Yi said, "Looking at current affairs recently, there is much effort at adjustment and protection, but little intent to support and uphold; this is not to the court's advantage."

sentences.zh: 嘉、敘、瀘俱接夷壤，董蠻米在大入，俘殺兵民，四路創安邊司窮治其事。

translations.literal: Jia, Xu, and Lu all bordered barbarian territory. Dong Manmi of the Mi barbarians made a major incursion, capturing and killing soldiers and civilians, and the four circuits created the Pacify the Border Office to investigate the matter thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Jia, Xu, and Lu all bordered barbarian territory. Dong Manmi of the Mi barbarians made a major incursion, capturing and killing soldiers and civilians, and the four circuits created the Pacify the Border Office to investigate the matter thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 奕得夷人質之以致所掠，由是迕安邊司。

translations.literal: Yi took barbarian hostages in order to recover what had been plundered, and because of this he offended the Pacify the Border Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took barbarian hostages in order to recover what had been plundered, and because of this he offended the Pacify the Border Office.

sentences.zh: 夷酋王粲浮檆木萬計入賈，奕慮其蕩水陸之險，驅之。

translations.literal: The barbarian chief Wang Can floated tens of thousands of cedar logs in for sale; Yi feared they would break down the defenses by water and land, and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian chief Wang Can floated tens of thousands of cedar logs in for sale; Yi feared they would break down the defenses by water and land, and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 安撫使安丙新立大功，讒忌日聞，宰相錢象祖出謗書問奕，奕喟而言：「士不愛一死而因於眾多之口，亦可悲也。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner An Bing had newly achieved great merit; slander and jealousy were heard daily; Chief Minister Qian Xiangzu produced slander books and asked Yi; Yi sighed and said: 'A gentleman not loving one death yet trapped by many mouths is also pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner An Bing had newly achieved great merit; slander and jealousy were heard daily. Chief Minister Qian Xiangzu produced slander books and asked Yi; Yi sighed and said, 'A gentleman who will not risk one death yet is trapped by many mouths is pitiable.

sentences.zh: 奕願以百口保之。」

translations.literal: Yi wished to guarantee him with a hundred mouths.'
translations.idiomatic: Yi offered to guarantee him with a hundred lives.'

sentences.zh: 象祖艴然曰：「公悉安子文若此乎？」

translations.literal: Xiangzu flushed and said: 'Do you all trust An Ziwen thus?'
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzu flushed and said: 'Do you all trust An Ziwen thus?'

sentences.zh: 適宇文紹節宣撫荊湖還，亦曰：「僕願亦百口以信許公之言。」

translations.literal: Just then Yuwen Shaojie returned from pacifying Jing-Hu and also said, "I too would pledge a hundred lives to support Lord Xu's words."
translations.idiomatic: Just then Yuwen Shaojie returned from pacifying Jing-Hu and also said, "I too would pledge a hundred lives to support Lord Xu's words."

sentences.zh: 於是異論頓息，委寄益專。

translations.literal: Thereupon dissenting arguments abruptly ceased, and the trust placed in An Bing became even more exclusive.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon dissenting arguments abruptly ceased, and the trust placed in An Bing became even more exclusive.

sentences.zh: 奕於丙深相知，而職事所關必反復辯數以求直。

translations.literal: Yi and An Bing knew each other deeply, but whenever official duties were involved, Yi always argued back and forth to seek what was right.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and An Bing knew each other deeply, but whenever official duties were involved, Yi always argued back and forth to seek what was right.

sentences.zh: 其後士多畔丙，奕獨以書疏候問愈數。

translations.literal: Afterward many scholars turned against Bing, but Yi alone sent him letters and memorials asking after him all the more often.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward many scholars turned against Bing, but Yi alone sent him letters and memorials asking after him all the more often.

sentences.zh: 移知夔州，表辭不行，改知遂寧府。

translations.literal: Transferred to be prefect of Kuizhou, he submitted a memorial declining and did not go; he was changed to prefect of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to be prefect of Kuizhou, he submitted a memorial declining and did not go; he was changed to prefect of Suining.

sentences.zh: 捐緡錢數十萬以代民輸，復鹽策之利以養士，為浮梁作隄數百丈，民德之，畫像祠於學。

translations.literal: He donated several hundred thousand strings of cash to pay the people's levies for them, restored the profits from salt policy to support scholars, and built several hundred zhang of embankment for a floating bridge; the people were grateful and painted his image for a shrine in the school.
translations.idiomatic: He donated several hundred thousand strings of cash to pay the people's levies for them, restored the profits from salt policy to support scholars, and built several hundred zhang of embankment for a floating bridge; the people were grateful and painted his image for a shrine in the school.

sentences.zh: 進龍圖閣待制，加寶謨閣直學士，知潼川府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to waiting appointee of the Dragon Diagram Hall, given the added title direct academician of the Treasured Plans Hall, and made prefect of Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to waiting appointee of the Dragon Diagram Hall, given the added title direct academician of the Treasured Plans Hall, and made prefect of Tongchuan.

sentences.zh: 霖雨壞城，撤而築之，不以煩民，亦捐緡錢十二萬為十縣民代輸，於是其民亦相與祠於東山僧舍。

translations.literal: Continuous rain damaged the city wall; he dismantled and rebuilt it without troubling the people, and also donated 120,000 strings to pay levies for the people of ten counties. Thereupon those people too joined together to shrine him at the East Mountain monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Continuous rain damaged the city wall; he dismantled and rebuilt it without troubling the people, and also donated 120,000 strings to pay levies for the people of ten counties. Thereupon those people too joined together to shrine him at the East Mountain monastery.

sentences.zh: 會金人敗盟，蜀道震擾，奕請速選威望大臣宣撫，信賞必罰，以獎忠義、收人心。

translations.literal: When the Jin broke the treaty and the Shu routes were shaken and disturbed, Yi requested the swift selection of a senior minister with authority and reputation as pacification commissioner, with trustworthy rewards and certain punishments, in order to encourage loyalty and righteousness and gather people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin broke the treaty and the Shu routes were shaken and disturbed, Yi requested the swift selection of a senior minister with authority and reputation as pacification commissioner, with trustworthy rewards and certain punishments, in order to encourage loyalty and righteousness and gather people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 又言：「忠義之招，體勢倒持，兵食頓增，未知攸濟，且斬將之人未聞褒擢，敗軍之將未見施行，事勢不決，將有後時之悔。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'The summons of loyalty and righteousness—in posture it is upside down; army provisions suddenly increase—how to provide is unknown; moreover those who beheaded generals are not heard rewarded, defeated generals are not seen punished—affairs cannot be decided and there will be later regret.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'The summons of loyalty and righteousness holds power upside down; army provisions suddenly increase with no clear way to supply them; moreover those who beheaded generals are not heard rewarded, and defeated generals are not seen punished—if affairs cannot be decided, there will be later regret.'

sentences.zh: 御史劾奕欺罔，降一官。

translations.literal: The censor impeached Yi for deception and he was demoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: The censor impeached Yi for deception and he was demoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 詔提舉玉降宮，未數月，特復元官，提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: Edict made him director of the Jade Descent Palace; within not many months he was specially restored to original rank and made director of the Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him director of the Jade Descent Palace; within not many months he was specially restored to his original rank and made director of the Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 還家，草遺表曰：「自念本非衰病，初染微屙。

translations.literal: Returning home, he drafted a final memorial: "Reflecting on myself, I was not originally weakened by age; at first I caught only a slight illness.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home, he drafted a final memorial: "Reflecting on myself, I was not originally weakened by age; at first I caught only a slight illness.

sentences.zh: 當湯熨可去之時，臣以疾而為諱；

translations.literal: When hot compresses could have removed it, your servant concealed the illness;
translations.idiomatic: When hot compresses could have removed it, your servant concealed the illness;

sentences.zh: 及針石已窮之後，醫束手而莫圖。

translations.literal: but after acupuncture and cautery had been exhausted, the physicians folded their hands and had no plan.
translations.idiomatic: but after acupuncture and cautery had been exhausted, the physicians folded their hands and had no plan.

sentences.zh: 靖言膏肓所致之由，大抵脈絡不通之故。」

translations.literal: Quiet words on the deep illness's cause—mostly because the pulse channels were not connected.'
translations.idiomatic: Quiet words on the deep illness's cause—mostly because the pulse channels were not connected.'

sentences.zh: 皆寓諷諫之意。

translations.literal: All embodied allegorical remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: All embodied allegorical remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 進顯謨閣直學士致仕，贈通議大夫。

translations.literal: Promoted to Direct Bearer of the Manifest Illustrious Hall and retired; posthumously given Master of Discussion on Government.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Bearer of the Manifest Illustrious Hall and retired, and was posthumously given the title Master of Discussion on Government.

sentences.zh: 初，奕之守瀘，帝顧禮部尚書章穎曰：「許奕已去乎？」

translations.literal: At first when Yi governed Lu, the emperor turned to Minister of Rites Zhang Ying and said: 'Has Xu Yi already left?'
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was governing Lu, the emperor turned to Minister of Rites Zhang Ying and asked, 'Has Xu Yi already left?'

sentences.zh: 起居舍人真德秀侍帝前，論人才，上以骨鯁稱之。

translations.literal: Recorder of the emperor's actions Zhen Dexiu attended before the emperor and discussed talent; the emperor praised him as backbone.
translations.idiomatic: Recorder of the emperor's actions Zhen Dexiu attended before the emperor and discussed talent; the emperor praised him as backbone.

sentences.zh: 奕天性孝友，送死恤孤，恩意備至。

translations.literal: Yi by nature was filial and friendly; in sending off the dead and comforting orphans his kindness was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was by nature filial and friendly; in sending off the dead and comforting orphans his kindness was complete.

sentences.zh: 通籀隸書，所著有《毛詩說》、《論語尚書周禮講義》、奏議、雜文行世。

translations.literal: He mastered seal, official, and clerical script; his works include Explanations of the Mao Odes, Expositions on the Analects, Documents, and Zhou Rites, memorials, and miscellaneous writings current in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered seal, official, and clerical script; his works include Explanations of the Mao Odes, Expositions on the Analects, Documents, and Zhou Rites, memorials, and miscellaneous writings current in the world.

sentences.zh: 陳居仁

translations.literal: Chen Juren
translations.idiomatic: Chen Juren

sentences.zh: 陳居仁，字安行，興化軍人。

translations.literal: Chen Juren, styled Anxing, was a native of Xinghua commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Juren, whose courtesy name was Anxing, came from Xinghua commandery.

sentences.zh: 父太府少卿膏，娶明州汪氏女，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Gao married a woman of the Wang clan of Ming Prefecture and therefore made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Chen Gao, married a woman of the Wang clan of Ming Prefecture and therefore made his home there.

sentences.zh: 膏初為汾州教授，佐守臣張克戩捍金人。

translations.literal: His father Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Gao married a woman of the Wang clan of Ming Prefecture and therefore made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Gao married a woman of the Wang clan of Ming Prefecture and therefore made his home there.

sentences.zh: 後知惠州，單馬造曾袞壘，譬曉降之。

translations.literal: Gao at first was professor of Fen Prefecture and assisted the defending minister Zhang Kechan in resisting the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Gao at first was professor of Fen Prefecture and assisted the defending minister Zhang Kechan in resisting the Jin.

sentences.zh: 鄞僧王法恩謀逆事覺，或請屠城，膏方為御史，力論多殺非聖世事，脅從者悉寬宥之。

translations.literal: The Yin monk Wang Fa'en's plot of rebellion was discovered; some requested slaughtering the city—Gao was then censor and forcefully argued that mass killing was not a sagely-age affair; those coerced were all leniently pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin monk Wang Fa'en's plot of rebellion was discovered; some requested slaughtering the city—Gao was then censor and forcefully argued that mass killing was not a sagely-age affair; those coerced were all leniently pardoned.

sentences.zh: 居仁年十四而孤，以蔭授鉛山尉。

translations.literal: Juren at fourteen was orphaned; by yin privilege he was appointed assistant magistrate of Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Juren was orphaned at fourteen; by yin privilege he was appointed assistant magistrate of Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十一年舉進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Shaoxing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Shaoxing (1151) he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 秦檜與膏有故，有勸以一見可得美官，居仁曰：「是有命焉。」

translations.literal: Qin Hui and Gao had old ties; some urged one meeting to obtain a fine office—Juren said: 'This has fate.'
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui and Gao had old ties; some urged one meeting to obtain a fine office—Juren said, 'This is a matter of fate.'

sentences.zh: 終不自通。

translations.literal: In the end he did not present himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not present himself.

sentences.zh: 移永豐令，入監行在點檢贍軍激賞酒庫所糴場，詔修《高宗聖政》，妙選寮屬，與范成大並充檢討官。

translations.literal: He was moved to magistrate of Yongfeng, entered as supervisor of the Capital Provision Army Reward Wine Warehouse purchase field, and by edict revised Sagely Governance of Gaozong; finely selected staff members—he and Fan Chengda were both made revising officers.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to magistrate of Yongfeng, entered as supervisor of the Capital Provision Army Reward Wine Warehouse purchase field, and by edict revised Sagely Governance of Gaozong; he and Fan Chengda were both made revising officers.

sentences.zh: 淮甸交兵，魏杞以宗正少卿使金，辟居仁幕下。

translations.literal: War was joined in the Huai region; Wei Qi, as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, was sent as envoy to Jin and recruited Juren to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When fighting broke out along the Huai, Wei Qi went to Jin as envoy with the rank of Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court and took Juren onto his mission staff.

sentences.zh: 時和戰未決，金兵駐淮北，人情恟懼，突騎大至，彎弓夾道，居仁上馬，猶從容舉酒屬杞：「天寒且酹此觴。」

translations.literal: At the time peace and war were undecided; Jin troops were stationed north of the Huai; popular feeling was alarmed and fearful; sudden cavalry arrived in force, bows bent lining both sides of the road; Juren mounted his horse and still calmly raised wine and entrusted it to Qi: "The weather is cold—let us libate with this cup."
translations.idiomatic: Peace and war were still unsettled, Jin armies held the north bank of the Huai, and fear ran through the mission. Enemy horsemen suddenly poured in, bows drawn along the road. Juren mounted and still calmly offered Qi a cup: "It is cold—drink this toast first."

sentences.zh: 觀者壯之。

translations.literal: Those who watched were heartened by him.
translations.idiomatic: The onlookers took heart at his bearing.

sentences.zh: 乃諭金人開道入，卒成禮，減歲幣而還。

translations.literal: Then he instructed the Jin to clear a road for entry; in the end the rites were completed and they returned having reduced the annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded the Jin to open a passage, the embassy rituals were completed, and the party returned having secured a reduction in annual tribute payments.

sentences.zh: 因出疆賞，轉承議郎，授諸王宮大小學教授。

translations.literal: Because of the border-mission reward he was transferred to Gentleman for Discussion of Policy and appointed professor of the great and small schools of the imperial princes' palace.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded for the border mission, he was promoted to Gentleman for Discussion of Policy and appointed to teach in the great and small schools of the princes' household.

sentences.zh: 杞秉國柄，居仁忍貧需遠次，未嘗求進。

translations.literal: Qi held national power; Juren bore poverty and waited in distant postings, never once seeking advancement.
translations.idiomatic: While Qi wielded state power, Juren endured poverty in remote assignments and never asked for promotion.

sentences.zh: 虞允文欲引以為用，不就。

translations.literal: Yu Yunwen wished to bring him into service; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen tried to draw him into office, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 允文欲與論兵，謝不能，退而貽書謂：「有定力乃可立事，若徒為大言，終必無成，幸成亦旋敗。」

translations.literal: Yunwen wished to discuss military affairs with him; he declined, unable; withdrawing he sent a letter saying: "Only with settled resolve can affairs be accomplished; if one merely utters grand words, in the end there will be no success—even if by chance there is success it will soon fail."
translations.idiomatic: When Yunwen wanted to debate military strategy, he pleaded incapacity, then wrote afterward: "Only steadfast resolve can establish real achievement. Grand talk alone ends in failure; even a fleeting success soon collapses."

sentences.zh: 允文為之色動。

translations.literal: Yunwen was moved in countenance by this.
translations.idiomatic: Yunwen visibly changed expression at the rebuke.

sentences.zh: 徙主軍器監簿、宗正修玉牒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as recorder of the Directorate of Military Equipment and to revise the imperial genealogy in the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to serve as registrar of the Directorate of Military Equipment and to edit the imperial genealogy for the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 轉對，言：「立國須定規模，陛下非無可致之資，而規模未立。」

translations.literal: At a rotation audience he said: "To found the state one must fix a model; Your Majesty is not without resources that could be brought to fruition, yet the model has not been fixed."
translations.idiomatic: At a palace audience he said: "A state must have a settled design. Your Majesty has the capacity to achieve great things, but that design has not yet been fixed."

sentences.zh: 孝宗初頗不懌，曰：「朕未嘗不立規模。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong at first was rather displeased and said: "I have not failed to establish a model."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was at first annoyed. "I have never failed to set a plan," he said.

sentences.zh: 居仁奏：「陛下銳意恢復，繼乃通和，和、戰、守三者迄今未定，孰為規模耶？」

translations.literal: Juren memorialized: "Your Majesty was keen to recover territory, then afterward pursued peace; peace, war, and defense—the three remain undecided to this day—which is the model?"
translations.idiomatic: Juren replied: "Your Majesty first pressed recovery, then turned to peace. War, peace, and defense are still unsettled. Which of these is your governing plan?"

sentences.zh: 允文曰：「此正前日定力之論，某今益知此言之當也。」

translations.literal: Yunwen said: "This is exactly the earlier argument on settled resolve; I now all the more know how fitting these words are."
translations.idiomatic: Yunwen said, "This is precisely what he meant about resolve. I see now how right he was."

sentences.zh: 遷將作監丞，轉國子丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, then became Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 九年，進秘書丞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he advanced to Secretary Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the reign he was promoted to Secretary Assistant.

sentences.zh: 入對，論文武並用長久之術：「陛下獎進武臣，深得持平救偏之道，然未必得智謀勇略之士，或多便佞輕躁之徒，將復有偏勝之患。」

translations.literal: Entering audience he discussed the long-term method of employing civil and military together: "Your Majesty's promotion and reward of military officers deeply grasp the way of balance to correct bias, yet one may not necessarily obtain men of wisdom, stratagem, courage, and design—or there may be many fawning, deceitful, frivolous, and rash persons; there will again be the harm of partial excess."
translations.idiomatic: In audience he urged a lasting balance of civil and military talent: "Your Majesty's encouragement of military men rightly corrects past bias, yet you may not be gaining true strategists, but rather sycophants and hotheads—and bias may return in another form."

sentences.zh: 帝喜納。

translations.literal: The Emperor happily accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed the advice.

sentences.zh: 權禮部郎官。

translations.literal: He served as Acting Secretariat Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served in an acting capacity as a director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 嘗言臺閣宜多用明習典故之士，帝問其人，居仁以李燾、莫濟對。

translations.literal: He once said the terrace offices ought to employ many men clearly versed in precedent and antiquity; the Emperor asked who they were, and Juren answered with Li Tao and Mo Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that the central archives should rely more on scholars versed in precedent. When the emperor asked for names, Juren recommended Li Tao and Mo Ji.

sentences.zh: 甫數日，召燾。

translations.literal: Only a few days later, Tao was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Li Tao was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 居仁力請外，乃知徽州。

translations.literal: Juren urgently requested an outside post and was then made prefect of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Juren pressed for a provincial post and was appointed prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 帝令陛辭，慰諭遣之。

translations.literal: The Emperor had him take leave at court, consoled and instructed him, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received his farewell audience, comforted him, and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 至郡，告以天子節經費以惠儉瘠，不能推廣聖德，吏則有罪。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the prefecture he announced that the Son of Heaven economized expenditures to benefit the frugal and impoverished; if he could not extend sagely virtue, the clerks were guilty.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the prefecture he announced that the emperor was cutting spending to help the poor, and that any official who failed to carry out that policy would be held guilty.

sentences.zh: 乃招三衙軍，植二表於庭，有輸納中度而遭抑退者，抱所輸立表下，親視之，人無留滯，吏不能措手，輸稅者恒裹贏以歸。

translations.literal: Then he summoned the three Yamen militia, planted two markers in the courtyard; those who had paid in correct measure but were rejected and sent back would embrace what they had paid and stand beneath the markers; he personally inspected them; none were detained; clerks could not lay hands on the process; taxpayers always wrapped up surplus and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the local militia offices and set up two posts in the courtyard. Anyone whose tax payment met the standard but was still turned away could stand under the posts holding his grain while Juren watched in person. No payment was held up and clerks could not interpose; taxpayers regularly went home with grain still tied in their bundles.

sentences.zh: 鄰州有訟，多詣臺省乞決於居仁。

translations.literal: Neighboring prefectures had lawsuits; many went to the terrace offices begging that Juren decide them.
translations.idiomatic: Litigants from neighboring prefectures often petitioned the central offices to have their cases decided by Juren.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，邦人挽留，由間道始得去。

translations.literal: When his term expired, the people of the prefecture detained him; only by a hidden path was he able to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended the people tried to keep him, and he escaped only by a back road.

sentences.zh: 入對，帝舉新安之政獎之。

translations.literal: Entering audience, the Emperor cited the government of Xin'an and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor praised his administration in Xin'an (Huizhou).

sentences.zh: 請編類隆興以來寬恤詔令，有曰：「法久則易玩，事久則易怠。

translations.literal: He requested compilation and classification of clemency edicts since Longxing, saying: "When laws are long-standing they are easily trifled with; when affairs are long-standing they are easily neglected.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that leniency edicts since the Longxing era be compiled, saying, "Laws grow stale and people treat them lightly; policies grow old and officials grow slack.

sentences.zh: 惟申加戒飭，有以儆其觀聽，則千萬年猶一日。」

translations.literal: Only if warnings and admonitions are repeatedly applied, having means to warn what is seen and heard, then even ten thousand years will be as one day."
translations.idiomatic: Repeated admonition keeps everyone alert, and then even after centuries the spirit of the law remains as fresh as on the first day."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「名言也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "These are famous words."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 又言：「歸正忠順，過於優渥，而遇戰士反輕。

translations.literal: He also said: "Those who turned loyal and submitted have been treated with excessive favor, yet those who met warriors in battle are instead slighted.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Defectors from the north are treated too generously, while men who actually fought are slighted.

sentences.zh: 此曹出萬死策勳，今老矣，添差已罷，廩稍半給，至丐於市，軍士解體。

translations.literal: These men emerged from myriad deaths to achieve merit; now they are old; supplementary assignments have ceased; ration stipends are half paid; they reach beggary in the markets—the soldiers' discipline dissolves.
translations.idiomatic: These men earned honors at the risk of their lives, but now in old age their extra appointments have ended, half their grain allowance is cut off, and some beg in the markets—the army's morale is collapsing.

sentences.zh: 乞加優恤，以終始念功之意，堅後生圖報之心。」

translations.literal: I beg increased generous care, so as to complete the intent of remembering merit from beginning to end and to stiffen the hearts of the young in plotting reward."
translations.idiomatic: He asked for better care for veterans, to honor merit to the end and stiffen younger soldiers' will to serve."

sentences.zh: 帝覽之嘉歎。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it and praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and praised it warmly.

sentences.zh: 會駕大閱白石，即命再添差兩任，衣糧全給，三軍為之呼舞。

translations.literal: It happened that the imperial carriage conducted a great review at Baishi; he immediately ordered two more supplementary assignments and full clothing and grain; the three armies shouted and danced for it.
translations.idiomatic: During a grand military review at Baishi the emperor immediately granted veterans two more supplementary appointments and full rations, and the armies cheered.

sentences.zh: 留為戶部右曹郎官，命未下，朝方推《會要》賞，帝曰：「陳居仁治行為天下第一，可因是並賞之。」

translations.literal: He was retained as Secretariat Director of the right bureau of the Ministry of Revenue; the appointment had not yet been issued when the court was just recommending rewards for the Essentials of Institutions; the Emperor said: "Chen Juren's governing conduct is first under Heaven—he may be rewarded together on this account."
translations.idiomatic: He was kept at court as a director in the Ministry of Revenue; before the order issued, the court was discussing rewards for work on the Essentials of Institutions. The emperor said, "Chen Juren's record as an administrator is the finest in the realm—reward him along with the others."

sentences.zh: 特轉朝議大夫兼權度支，又兼權禮部。

translations.literal: Specially transferred to Grandee of Court Discussion and concurrently Acting Director of Expenditure Control, and again concurrently Acting Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to Grandee of Court Discussion, with concurrent acting appointments in fiscal control and the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 會樞屬闕員，方進擬，帝曰：「豈有人才如陳居仁而可久為郎乎？」

translations.literal: It happened that the Bureau of Military Affairs had vacant posts and nominations were being advanced; the Emperor said: "Can there be talent like Chen Juren yet long remain a director?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Bureau of Military Affairs had openings and nominees were being listed, the emperor said, "How can someone of Chen Juren's talent stay in a mid-level post any longer?"

sentences.zh: 即授樞密院檢詳文字，尋為右司，遷左司，又遷檢正中書門下省諸房公事，歷兼左藏諸庫。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed textual reviewer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, soon right section; promoted to left section, again promoted to reviewer of the various bureaus of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and in sequence concurrently held the various treasuries of the left storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately made textual reviewer in the Bureau of Military Affairs, then right section chief, left section chief, and reviewer of Secretariat affairs, while also overseeing the left storehouse treasuries in turn.

sentences.zh: 居仁親視按牘，嘗謂：「有罪幸免則冤者何告，誣枉者七人皆當敘復。」

translations.literal: Juren personally inspected and checked documents; he once said: "If the guilty escape through leniency, to whom do the wronged appeal? Seven who were falsely accused should all be restored in rank."
translations.idiomatic: Juren personally reviewed case files and once said, "If the guilty go free, the innocent have nowhere to turn. Seven men were wrongfully convicted and should all be rehabilitated."

sentences.zh: 執政難之，居仁退，疏其冤狀上之。

translations.literal: The chief ministers found it difficult; Juren withdrew and memorialized the facts of their injustice upward.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers resisted, so Juren withdrew and sent up a memorial detailing the injustice.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「居仁精審，尚復何疑。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Juren is meticulous in examination—what doubt remains?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Juren has examined the case carefully. What further doubt is there?"

sentences.zh: 詔以旱求言，居仁乞命公卿務行寬大，御史京鏜極論從窄之弊，此風未革。

translations.literal: An edict because of drought sought advice; Juren begged that dukes and ministers be ordered to practice breadth; the censor Jing Chuan exhaustively discussed the harms of narrowness—this tendency was not yet reformed.
translations.idiomatic: After a drought edict inviting criticism, Juren urged the chief ministers to govern leniently, while Censor Jing Chuan had already attacked narrow severity—the habit had not yet changed.

sentences.zh: 假吏部尚書使金，還，遷起居郎，尋兼詳定一司敕令兼權中書舍人，泛恩濫賞，封繳無所避。

translations.literal: Acting as Minister of Personnel he was sent as envoy to Jin; on return he was promoted to Attendant Gentleman, soon concurrently revising the edicts of one office and concurrently Acting Secretariat Drafting Gentleman; broad grace and reckless rewards—he sealed and returned without avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: As acting Minister of Personnel he went on embassy to Jin. Back at court he became Attendant Gentleman, then helped revise the legal code and served as acting drafting secretary. Faced with indiscriminate favors and lavish rewards, he returned objection memorials without flinching.

sentences.zh: 因言：「恩惠不及小民，名為寬逋負，實以惠頑民耳；

translations.literal: Accordingly he said: "Favor does not reach the common people; named relief of arrears, in reality it favors the stubborn people only;
translations.idiomatic: He said, "These favors never reach ordinary people. What is called forgiving tax arrears really only helps defiant landowners;

sentences.zh: 名為赦有罪，實以惠姦民耳。

translations.literal: named amnesty of the guilty, in reality it favors treacherous people only.
translations.idiomatic: what is called pardoning criminals really only helps vicious offenders.

sentences.zh: 願盡放天下五等戶身丁，四等戶一半。」

translations.literal: I wish utterly to release household corvée for fifth-class households throughout the realm and half for fourth-class households."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that corvée service be canceled entirely for fifth-rank households nationwide and halved for fourth-rank households."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 安定王子肜乞封妾為夫人，居仁繳奏，帝喜迎，謂有補風教。

translations.literal: The Prince of Anding's son Xin requested ennobling a concubine as madame; Juren sealed and returned the memorial; the Emperor happily received it and said it aided popular custom and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Anding's son Xin asked to ennoble a concubine as a lady, Juren returned the draft. The emperor welcomed the objection and said it upheld public morals.

sentences.zh: 又論：「君人之道，貴在執要，今陛下親細故而忽遠猷，事末節而忘大體，願舉綱要以御臣下，省思慮以頤精神。」

translations.literal: He also argued: "The way of a ruler lies in holding essentials; now Your Majesty personally attends to minor details yet neglects distant plans, serves small nodes yet forgets the great form—I wish you would raise the net's head to control ministers below and reduce anxious thought to nourish the spirit."
translations.idiomatic: He also warned, "A ruler must grasp essentials. Your Majesty now busies yourself with trifles and neglects far-reaching policy, fusses over details and loses sight of the whole. Take hold of the main lines of governance and spare your energy."

sentences.zh: 詰旦，令清中書之務。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day he ordered clearance of Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the emperor ordered the Secretariat to clear its minor business.

sentences.zh: 權直學士院。

translations.literal: Acting duty at the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「內外制向委數人，今陳居仁一人當之，不見其難。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Internal and external documents were formerly entrusted to several men; now Chen Juren alone undertakes them and one does not see difficulty."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Court documents used to be split among several writers. Chen Juren handles them alone, and he shows no strain."

sentences.zh: 乞詔大臣博議「絕浮費，汰冗兵，計當省之數，定蠲除之目，此富民之要術也。」

translations.literal: He begged an edict that grand ministers broadly deliberate: "Cut floating expenses, reduce redundant troops, calculate numbers that should be saved, fix categories for remission and abolition—this is the essential art of enriching the people."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the emperor to have senior ministers debate how to end wasteful spending, cut redundant troops, set concrete savings targets, and define tax reductions—"the essential means to make the people prosper."

sentences.zh: 以集英殿修撰知鄂州，築長隄捍江，新安樂寮以養貧病之民，撥閒田歸之。

translations.literal: As Academician-Reviser of the Hall for Assembling Excellence he was made prefect of E Prefecture; he built a long dike to hold back the river; he newly established Joy Lodge to nurture the poor and sick, and assigned idle fields to it.
translations.idiomatic: As Academician-Reviser of the Hall for Assembling Excellence he governed E Prefecture, built a long dike against the Yangzi, founded a hospice for the poor and sick, and assigned vacant fields to support it.

sentences.zh: 進煥章閣待制，移建寧府。

translations.literal: He advanced to Attendant Academic Administrator of the Hall of Glorious Patterns and moved to Jianning prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Attendant Academic Administrator of the Hall of Glorious Patterns, he was transferred to Jianning.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，出儲粟平其價，弛逋負以巨萬計，代輸畸零繭稅。

translations.literal: The year was famine; he released stored grain to level prices, relaxed arrears amounting to tens of thousands, and paid irregular fragmentary cocoon taxes on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he sold reserve grain to stabilize prices, forgave millions in tax arrears, and paid fragmentary silk-tax debts for the people.

sentences.zh: 有因告糴殺人者，會赦免，居仁曰：「此亂民也，釋之將覆出為惡。」

translations.literal: There was one who killed a man over grain petitioning; an amnesty coincided and would have spared him; Juren said: "This is a disorderly person; if released he will again emerge and do evil."
translations.idiomatic: A man who had killed someone during a food riot was spared by a general amnesty. Juren said, "He is a riotous criminal. If released he will harm the people again."

sentences.zh: 遂誅之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Juren had him executed anyway.

sentences.zh: 觀察推官柳某死，貧不克歸，二子行丐於道，聞而憐之，予之衣食，買田以養之，擇師以教之。

translations.literal: Investigative Commissioner Assessor Liu someone died; too poor to return home, his two sons begged along the road; Juren heard and pitied them, gave them clothing and food, bought fields to support them, and chose a teacher to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: When an investigative commission assessor surnamed Liu died too poor to send his body home, his two sons were begging on the road. Juren took pity, gave them food and clothing, bought land to support them, and found them a tutor.

sentences.zh: 鎮江大旱，又移居仁守鎮江。

translations.literal: Zhenjiang suffered great drought; again Juren was moved to govern Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: After a severe drought in Zhenjiang, Juren was transferred to govern that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 請以緡錢十四萬給兵食，不報；

translations.literal: He requested fourteen myriad strings of cash for soldiers' provisions; no reply;
translations.idiomatic: He requested 140,000 strings of cash for troop rations and received no answer;

sentences.zh: 為書以義撼丞相，然後許。

translations.literal: he wrote a letter using righteousness to move the chief councilor, and then it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: then wrote to the chief councilor on moral grounds and won approval.

sentences.zh: 發時密往覘之。

translations.literal: When it was issued he secretly went to observe it.
translations.idiomatic: When the grain was dispatched he went secretly to inspect the distribution.

sentences.zh: 間遣糴運於荊楚商人，商人曰：「是陳待制耶？」

translations.literal: Meanwhile he sent grain-purchase transport to merchants of Jing and Chu; a merchant said: "Is this Vice Commissioner Chen?"
translations.idiomatic: He also sent agents to buy grain from Hubei merchants, who asked, "Is this Commissioner Chen?"

sentences.zh: 爭以粟就糴。

translations.literal: They contended to offer grain for purchase.
translations.idiomatic: They competed to sell him their grain.

sentences.zh: 居仁區畫有方，所存活數萬計。

translations.literal: Juren partitioned and planned with method; those who were kept alive numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Juren organized relief effectively and kept tens of thousands alive.

sentences.zh: 因饑民治古海鮮界港，為石䃮丹徒境上，蓄泄以時，以通漕運。

translations.literal: Using famine people he repaired the ancient boundary harbor of Guanghai Fresh; in Dantu territory he made stone revetments, storing and releasing according to season, to open grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He employed famine refugees to restore the ancient Guanghai harbor, built stone embankments in Dantu, and regulated sluices on schedule to keep the grain transport route open.

sentences.zh: 治江陰姦僧。

translations.literal: He dealt with treacherous monks of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He prosecuted corrupt monks in Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 加寶文閣待制、知福州。

translations.literal: Added Attendant Academic Administrator of the Hall of Precious Culture and made prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Attendant Academic Administrator of the Hall of Precious Culture and appointed prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 入境，有饑民嘯聚，部分牙兵遮擊之，首惡計窮，自經死。

translations.literal: On entering the border there were hungry people who gathered shouting; he divided yamen troops to intercept and strike them; the chief villain's stratagems were exhausted and he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: On entering the prefecture he found starving people rioting in bands. He dispatched government troops to block them, and the ringleader, seeing no escape, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 治宗室之暴橫，申蠱毒之舊禁。

translations.literal: He dealt with the violent overbearing among the imperial clan; he reasserted the old prohibition on gu poison.
translations.idiomatic: He curbed lawless imperial clansmen and reimposed the old ban on poison cults.

sentences.zh: 有召命求閒者，再進華文閣直學士，提舉太平興國宮，卒，贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Having a summons he sought leisure; again advanced to Direct Academic Gentleman of the Literary Glory Hall, devoted attendant of the Taiping Xingguo Palace; he died and was posthumously given Grandee of the Purple Audience with the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: When there was a summons to court he asked for a quiet post, was again advanced to Direct Academician of Huawen Pavilion and superintendent of Taiping Xingguo Palace, and died. He was posthumously granted Grandee for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 居仁風度凝遠，處己應物，壹以誠信。

translations.literal: Juren's bearing was composed and distant; in treating himself and responding to things he was wholly with sincerity and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Juren's bearing was calm and reserved; in private conduct and public dealings alike he acted with complete integrity.

sentences.zh: 臨事毅然有守，所至號稱循吏，皆立祠祀之。

translations.literal: Facing affairs he was resolute and had integrity; wherever he arrived they were called orderly officials and all set up shrines to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was firm and principled. Everywhere he served he was hailed as a model administrator, and shrines were raised in his honor.

sentences.zh: 有奏議、制稿、詩文行世。

translations.literal: He had memorials, drafted edicts, and poetry and prose current in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials, draft edicts, poems, and essays circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 子卓。

translations.literal: His son Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo

sentences.zh: 子 卓

translations.literal: Son Zhuo
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo

sentences.zh: 卓，字立道，紹熙元年進士，其後知江州，移寧國府。

translations.literal: Zhuo, styled Lidao, passed the jinshi in the first year of Shaoxi; afterward he governed Jiang Prefecture and moved to Ningguo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo, courtesy name Lidao, passed the jinshi in 1190 and later governed Jiangzhou and Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 丞相以故欲見之，卓謝不往，丞相益器之。

translations.literal: The chief councilor because of old ties wished to see him; Zhuo declined and did not go; the chief councilor all the more treasured him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor, an old acquaintance, wished to see him, but Zhuo declined. The minister valued him all the more.

sentences.zh: 李全叛，褫其爵，詔書至淮，人益自勵；

translations.literal: Li Quan rebelled; his noble rank was stripped; the edict reached the Huai; people all the more encouraged themselves;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Quan rebelled, an edict stripping his titles reached the Huai front and stiffened public morale;

sentences.zh: 太廟災，降罪己詔，京師感動，皆卓所草也。

translations.literal: the Imperial Ancestral Temple burned; a self-blame edict was issued; the capital was deeply moved—all were drafted by Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: when fire destroyed the imperial ancestral temple, Zhuo also drafted the self-reproach edict that deeply moved the capital.

sentences.zh: 為簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: He served as concurrently signing secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丐祠還里。

translations.literal: Before long he begged a temple post and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked for a sinecure and returned home.

sentences.zh: 平生不營產業，以賛書所酬金築世綸堂。

translations.literal: All his life he did not manage estates; with gold paid for secretarial drafting he built the Hall of Generations of Brocade.
translations.idiomatic: He never built up property, and used his pay as a drafting secretary to erect the Shilun Hall.

sentences.zh: 閑居十有六年，卒年八十有六。

translations.literal: In retirement sixteen years; he died aged eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement sixteen years and died at eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 將葬，事不能具，丞相吳潛聞之，貽書制置使以助。

translations.literal: About to be buried, affairs could not be completed; Chief Councilor Wu Qian heard of it and sent a letter to the military commissioner to assist.
translations.idiomatic: When his family could not afford the funeral, Chief Councilor Wu Qian heard and wrote the prefectural commissioner to help.

sentences.zh: 其孫定孫力請諡於朝，乃諡「清敏」。

translations.literal: His grandson Dingsun forcefully requested a posthumous title at court; thereupon he was titled "Pure and Alert."
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Dingsun pressed the court for a posthumous title, and Zhuo was given the name Qingmin, "Pure and Vigilant."

sentences.zh: 劉漢弼

translations.literal: Liu Hanbi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanbi

sentences.zh: 劉漢弼，字正甫，上虞人。

translations.literal: Liu Hanbi, styled Zhengfu, was a native of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanbi, courtesy name Zhengfu, came from Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 生二歲而孤，母謝氏撫而教之。

translations.literal: At two years of age he was orphaned; his mother the Lady Xie nurtured and taught him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at two, he was raised and educated by his mother, Lady Xie.

sentences.zh: 嘉定九年舉進士，授吉州教授。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiading he passed the jinshi and was appointed professor of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1216 he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed professor at Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷江西安撫司幹官，監南嶽廟、浙西提舉茶鹽司幹官。

translations.literal: He served as staff officer of the Jiangxi Pacification Commission, supervised the Southern Marchmount Temple, and staff officer of the Western Zhe Tea and Salt Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the Jiangxi Pacification Commission staff, as superintendent of the Southern Marchmount Temple, and on the Western Zhe tea and salt intendant staff.

sentences.zh: 召試館職，改秘書省正字，序遷秘書郎兼沂王府教授，改著作佐郎兼史館校勘，權考功員外郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned to an examination for a Hanlin post, changed to Rectifier in the Secretariat, advanced in order to Secretariat Gentleman and concurrently professor of the Prince of Yi's palace, changed to Assistant Compiler and concurrently collator of the History Office, and Acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to a qualifying examination for the Hanlin Academy, he became Secretariat Rectifier, rose to Secretariat Gentleman while teaching in the Prince of Yi's household, then became Assistant Compiler and History Office collator, and acting Vice Director of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 升著作郎、知嘉興府兼兵部員外郎，改兼考功。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Compiler and made prefect of Jiaxing while concurrently holding Vice Director of the Ministry of War, then changed to concurrent Vice Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Compiler, he governed Jiaxing while also serving as Vice Director of War, then shifted to a concurrent Personnel post.

sentences.zh: 尋為考功員外郎兼崇政殿說書、編修國史、檢討實錄，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: Soon he became Vice Director of Personnel and concurrently lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, compiler of the National History, collator of the Veritable Records, and was elevated to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Vice Director of Personnel, lectured at the Chongzheng Hall, compiled the National History and Veritable Records, and was promoted to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 出知溫州。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋擢太常少卿，以左司諫召，擢侍御史兼侍講，以戶部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: Soon he was elevated to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, summoned as Left Section Remonstrator, elevated to Attendant Censor and concurrently Lecturer, and retired as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, recalled as Left Section Remonstrator, then Attendant Censor and court lecturer, and retired as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 漢弼學明義利之辨，為正字時，應詔言事，極論致災弭災之道。

translations.literal: Hanbi's learning clarified the distinction of righteousness and profit; as Rectifier he responded to the edict on affairs and exhaustively discussed the ways to bring disaster and to quell disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Hanbi was learned in distinguishing righteousness from profit. As Secretariat Rectifier he answered the emperor's call for advice with a thorough discussion of how calamities arise and how they may be averted.

sentences.zh: 為校書郎，轉對，舉蘇軾所言結人心，厚風俗，存紀綱。

translations.literal: As collator, at court audience he cited Su Shi's words on binding people's hearts, thickening customs, and preserving standards.
translations.idiomatic: As collator, at court audience he cited Su Shi's words on binding people's hearts, thickening customs, and preserving standards.

sentences.zh: 又論制閫當復其舊，戎司當各還其所，邊郡守當用武臣。

translations.literal: He also discussed that pacification commissioners should be restored to their old posts, frontier commissions each returned to their places, and border prefectures should employ military officials.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that pacification commissioners should be restored to their old posts, frontier commissions returned to their proper places, and border prefectures should employ military officials.

sentences.zh: 又論決和戰以定國論，合江、淮以壹帥權，公賞罰以勵人心，廣規撫以用人才。

translations.literal: He also discussed deciding war and peace to settle the state's doctrine, uniting Jiang and Huai under one commander's authority, public rewards and punishments to stir people's hearts, and broad pacification to employ talent.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued for deciding war and peace to settle national policy, uniting Jiang and Huai under one commander's authority, using public rewards and punishments to stir hearts, and broad pacification to employ talent.

sentences.zh: 為著作佐郎，言兵財楮幣權不可分。

translations.literal: As assistant compiler he said military finances and paper currency authority must not be divided.
translations.idiomatic: As assistant compiler he said military finances and paper currency authority must not be divided.

sentences.zh: 又言取士之法，詞學不當去「宏博」字，混補不如復待補之便。

translations.literal: He also discussed the method of selecting scholars: the erudite phrases examination should not drop the word 'comprehensive and broad,' and mixed supplementary appointment was inferior to restoring waiting supplementary appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He also discussed examination policy: the erudite phrases category should keep the word 'comprehensive and broad,' and mixed supplementary appointment was inferior to restoring waiting supplementary appointment.

sentences.zh: 為著作，為考功員外，所陳皆切於時務。

translations.literal: As compiler and vice director of Personnel, what he presented all cut to current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As compiler and vice director of Personnel, everything he presented cut closely to current affairs.

sentences.zh: 及為言官，帝獎諭曰：「以卿純實不欺，故此親擢，宜悉心以告。」

translations.literal: When he became a remonstrating official, the emperor praised him: 'Because you are pure and solid without deception, I personally raised you—should fully devote heart to inform me.'
translations.idiomatic: When he became a remonstrating official, the emperor praised him: 'Because you are pure and solid without deception, I personally raised you—devote yourself fully to advising me.'

sentences.zh: 漢弼以臺綱久馳，疏三事，曰：定規撫，正體統，遠謀慮。

translations.literal: Hanbi, because censorial standards had long lapsed, memorialized three matters: settle pacification, correct institutional form, and keep distant counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Hanbi, because censorial standards had long lapsed, memorialized three matters: settle pacification, correct institutional form, and keep distant counsel.

sentences.zh: 首論給事中錢相巧於迎合，睥睨政地，直學士院吳愈不稱其職，罷去之。

translations.literal: First he discussed Reviewing Secretary Qian Xiang, skilled at flattery, eyeing political ground; Direct Bearer of the Academy Wu Yu did not fit his post—dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: First he discussed Reviewing Secretary Qian Xiang, skilled at flattery and eyeing political ground; Direct Bearer of the Academy Wu Yu did not fit his post—dismiss them.

sentences.zh: 又劾中書舍人濮斗南、左正言葉賁，疏留中不出。

translations.literal: He also impeached Drafting Secretary Pu Dounan and Left Rectifier Ye Ben; the memorial was held in the palace and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Drafting Secretary Pu Dounan and Left Rectifier Ye Ben; the memorial was held in the palace and not issued.

sentences.zh: 賁，松陽人，為時相史嵩之腹心。

translations.literal: Ben was a native of Songyang and the trusted confidant of Chief Minister Shi Songzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ben was a native of Songyang and the trusted confidant of Chief Minister Shi Songzhi.

sentences.zh: 有使賁互按者，明日賁有他命，而漢弼由是去國。

translations.literal: Someone had Ben conduct mutual investigation; the next day Ben received another appointment and Hanbi thereby left the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Someone had Ben conduct mutual investigation; the next day Ben received another appointment and Hanbi thereby left the capital.

sentences.zh: 嵩之久擅國柄，帝益患苦之，既復以左司諫召，首贊帝分別邪正以息眾疑。

translations.literal: Songzhi long monopolized state power; the emperor grew more troubled; having again summoned Hanbi as left remonstrator, he first praised the emperor's distinguishing depravity and rectitude to quiet many doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi long monopolized state power; the emperor grew more troubled; having again summoned Hanbi as left remonstrator, he first praised the emperor's distinguishing depravity and rectitude to quiet many doubts.

sentences.zh: 奏疏論立聖心、正君道、謹事機、伸士氣、收人才五事，帝嘉其言，並付外行之。

translations.literal: His memorial discussed establishing sagely heart, correcting ruler's way, careful handling of opportunities, extending scholar-official spirit, and gathering talent—five matters; the emperor praised his words and all were sent out for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial discussed establishing sagely heart, correcting the ruler's way, careful handling of opportunities, extending scholar-official spirit, and gathering talent—five matters; the emperor praised his words and all were sent out for implementation.

sentences.zh: 及為侍御史，密奏曰：「自古未有一日無宰相之朝，今虛相位已三月，尚可狐疑而不斷乎？

translations.literal: When he was attendant censor he secretly memorialized: 'From old there has never been a court for a single day without a chief minister; now the vacant phase has lasted three months—can one still hesitate without deciding?
translations.idiomatic: When he was attendant censor he secretly memorialized: 'From old there has never been a court for a single day without a chief minister; now the vacant phase has lasted three months—can one still hesitate without deciding?

sentences.zh: 願奮發英斷，拔去陰邪，庶可轉危而安；

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will rouse brilliant decision, uproot hidden depravity—then one may turn danger to safety;
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will rouse brilliant decision and uproot hidden depravity—then one may turn danger to safety;

sentences.zh: 否則是非不可兩立，邪正不並進，陛下雖欲收召善類，不可得矣。

translations.literal: otherwise right and wrong cannot stand together, depravity and rectitude cannot advance together—though Your Majesty wishes to gather good men, it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise right and wrong cannot stand together and depravity and rectitude cannot advance together—though Your Majesty wishes to gather good men, it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 臣聞富弼之起復，止於五請，蔣芾之起復，止於三請，今嵩之既六請矣，願聽其終喪，亟選賢臣，早定相位。」

translations.literal: Your servant hears Fu Bi's return from mourning stopped at five requests, Jiang Fu's at three—now Songzhi has already requested six; I hope to hear his full mourning, quickly select worthy ministers, and early settle the phase.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant hears Fu Bi's return from mourning stopped at five requests, Jiang Fu's at three—now Songzhi has already requested six; I hope to hear his full mourning, quickly select worthy ministers, and early settle the phase.'

sentences.zh: 帝覽納，遂決。

translations.literal: The emperor read and accepted it and thereupon decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read and accepted it and thereupon decided.

sentences.zh: 乃命范鍾、杜範並相，百官舉笏相慶，漢弼之力為多。

translations.literal: He then ordered Fan Zhong and Du Fan both as chief ministers; the hundred officials raised their tablets in mutual rejoicing—Hanbi's effort was great.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Fan Zhong and Du Fan both as chief ministers; the hundred officials raised their tablets in mutual rejoicing—Hanbi's effort was great.

sentences.zh: 又累章言金淵、鄭起潛、陳一薦、謝達、韓祥、濮斗南、王德明，皆疇昔託身私門，為之腹心，盤據要路，公論之所切齒者。

translations.literal: He also submitted successive memorials on Jin Yuan, Zheng Qiqian, Chen Yijian, Xie Da, Han Xiang, Pu Dounan, and Wang Deming—all formerly entrusting themselves to private gates as their heart-and-belly, occupying key roads, men of whom public opinion gnashed teeth.
